exhibitions.title: The Poor Man's Rembrandt Project
exhibitions.description: Tattoo artist Henk Schiffmacher and his team set up studio inside Rembrandt's house, inking original Rembrandt-inspired designs on visitors: the tattoo as the affordable old master.

exhibitions.title: The Land of Chocolate Sprinkles. Building a new world together
exhibitions.description: Congolese collective CATPC shows 30 sculptures cast in cacao, palm oil and sugar, plus embroideries on cacao sacks, funding the buy-back of exhausted plantation land.

exhibitions.title: Keerthana Kunnath - Not What You Saw
exhibitions.description: The London-based photographer's first museum exhibition, portraying female bodybuilders in Kerala with equal strength and softness to unsettle regional ideas of gender and beauty.

exhibitions.title: Middle East Archive - Al Nisa / Women
exhibitions.description: Two-part Foam project in Amsterdam-West: Yomna El Beyaly solo at Mercatorplein (to 29 Oct) and the group show Al Nisa / Women at MAQAM (to 20 Dec), curated by Romaisa Baddar.

exhibitions.title: the ESSENCE
exhibitions.description: A show tracing graffiti's cultural roots through names, tags, lines and repetition: the building blocks of a visual language born from movement and marking presence.

exhibitions.title: Experimental Urge
exhibitions.description: Over 80 works on paper, from Rembrandt to living artists, tracing how printmakers and draughtsmen kept pushing techniques and materials. Visitors can draw their own work in the gallery.

exhibitions.title: Marcos Kueh: PRESENT
exhibitions.description: Four woven tapestries by Malaysian textile artist Marcos Kueh in the Red Bedroom, a last love letter to his father that echoes the canopy of the empty four-poster bed.

exhibitions.title: Unfinished Pasts: Return, Keep, or...?
exhibitions.description: Steps into the live restitution debate, exploring dilemmas and stories behind contested colonial-era objects.

exhibitions.title: Yoshitoshi. Master of the Moon
exhibitions.description: Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's print series 'One Hundred Aspects of the Moon' shown at the Van Gogh Museum for the first time: warriors, lovers and mythical beings in bold colour.

exhibitions.title: Tales of Two by YONK
exhibitions.description: An interactive digital-puppetry installation by The Hague studio YONK, where visitors use gestures to guide animated characters into shared stories.

exhibitions.title: Whistler. Dandy and Disruptor
exhibitions.description: The first retrospective in the Netherlands devoted to James McNeill Whistler (1834–1903): painter, printmaker, aesthete and enfant terrible.

exhibitions.title: Rembrandt Open Studio
exhibitions.description: Fifth edition: artists Marije Gertenbach and Shani Leseman take over working studios inside Rembrandt's house, with visitors able to watch them at work from 13 November to 10 January.

exhibitions.title: Pioneers of Media Art: The First Years of MonteVideo
exhibitions.description: A group show with LI-MA tracing the first years of MonteVideo, the Netherlands' pioneering video-art gallery, from 1970s electronic imagery to today's immersive artists.

exhibitions.title: The Best Dutch Book Designs 2025
exhibitions.description: The annual selection of the best-designed Dutch books of 2025, chosen by a professional and a student jury, in the centenary year of the first selection.

exhibitions.title: Document Netherlands: New Energy
exhibitions.description: Photographer and filmmaker Kadir van Lohuizen documents the Dutch energy transition: towering wind turbines, thick undersea cables and colossal platforms on the open sea.

exhibitions.title: Yayoi Kusama
exhibitions.description: Landmark retrospective spanning more than seven decades of Kusama's work: painting, sculpture, installation, drawing, fashion, collage and happenings.

exhibitions.title: Adam Pendleton — Some Wild Kind of Language
exhibitions.description: Pendleton's first museum exhibition in the Netherlands: eleven paintings and eight large-scale drawings exploring abstract form, most of them never shown before.

exhibitions.title: Willem de Kooning at Work
exhibitions.description: A century after de Kooning left the Netherlands for New York, a retrospective of more than 120 drawings with celebrated paintings and sculptures, made with the Art Institute of Chicago.

exhibitions.title: Hailun Ma - Hometown
exhibitions.description: The Chinese photographer's first major solo show outside China: recent series on family, youth and daily style in Xinjiang, where fashion becomes a lens for social observation.

exhibitions.title: Myriam Boulos - A Collective Diary: Sexual Fantasies
exhibitions.description: First museum solo show of Lebanese photographer Myriam Boulos, 19th Foam Paul Huf Award winner: a collective diary centred on her series Sexual Fantasies, mostly made in Beirut.

exhibitions.title: Cabinet of Stories: Change the World, Not Us
exhibitions.description: A World Pride show drawing on the archaeology, book and theatre collections to surface forgotten LGBTIQ+ stories across history.

exhibitions.title: Nadav Kander - The Edge of Things
exhibitions.description: Four decades of Nadav Kander's photography, from his Prix Pictet-winning Yangtze River series to portraits of Obama and David Lynch, drawn together by fragility, time and quiet intensity.

exhibitions.title: Ulrich Seidl – Über das Leben, die Liebe und den Tod
exhibitions.description: The first comprehensive Dutch exhibition on Austrian filmmaker Ulrich Seidl, gathering early, little-known and newly commissioned film works about ordinary lives in late-capitalist society.

exhibitions.title: Adolphe de Meyer: The Substance of a Venetian Dream
exhibitions.description: The first European museum show of a rediscovered set of 75 photographs by fashion pioneer Adolphe de Meyer, documenting his life in Venice's Palazzo Balbi-Valier between 1904 and 1909.

exhibitions.title: Andrzej Steinbach: Hier
exhibitions.description: A first Dutch introduction to Andrzej Steinbach's meticulously composed photography, treating seeing itself as an aesthetic problem across typologically organised series.

exhibitions.title: Maya Inès Touam: Belongings
exhibitions.description: The French-Algerian artist's first solo Dutch museum show, presenting digital collages built from hundreds of photographs that explore migration, motherhood and displacement.

exhibitions.title: Hella de Jonge – Dichter bij hun ziel
exhibitions.description: 37 paintings and two sculptures by Hella de Jonge exploring war, family trauma and collective memory rooted in her Jewish family's history.

exhibitions.title: Chez Matisse - Masterpieces from Centre Pompidou
exhibitions.description: Over eighty works from the Centre Pompidou trace Matisse's hunt for balance between colour, form and simplicity, alongside Picasso, Rothko and Barnett Newman.

exhibitions.title: Play!
exhibitions.description: Hands-on pop-up on how games travel the world, from the 4,500-year-old Royal Game of Ur and Mahjong to Tetris and Mario, all playable.

exhibitions.title: Junk Space: Claiming Public Spaces
exhibitions.description: Artists reclaim the anonymous city of malls, infrastructure and forgotten corners, after Rem Koolhaas's "Junkspace", in a show made with Museum MORE.

exhibitions.title: Amsterdam – A Work of Art
exhibitions.description: Iconic 17th-century cityscapes showing how Amsterdam depicted itself as a wealthy, innovative world power as it transformed into a global trading hub.

exhibitions.title: Art Is Not a Crime
exhibitions.description: Photographer Henry Chalfant's documentation of graffiti culture, curated by SUSO33 with archival material from the Dutch Graffiti Library linking his lens to the Dutch graffiti scene.

exhibitions.title: WORN: Treasured Clothing
exhibitions.description: Twenty-four worn, altered and reused garments dating from 1640 to 1930, from embroidered 17th-century mules to a dress passed down through generations of the Six family.

exhibitions.title: Vincent Ruijters - Crimson Gilt
exhibitions.description: An installation of more than a thousand knitted strips in gold and crimson conjures the ghost of the East Indiaman Amsterdam: gold for trade and prosperity, red for colonialism and exploitation.

exhibitions.title: Abracadabra: Mysteries from Houdini to Hans Klok
exhibitions.venue: Joods Museum (Jewish Museum, Jewish Cultural Quarter)
exhibitions.description: The golden age of magic through its Jewish illusionists, from Harry Houdini to Hans Klok, with tricks visitors can try themselves.

exhibitions.title: Do It Yourself! On Cassette
exhibitions.description: Free mini-show in the museum's Studio on Dutch DIY cassette culture, from VPRO's Radiola Improvisatie Salon to the Carcassettes label, with clips to listen to.

exhibitions.title: Stephan Vanfleteren - Transcripts of a Sea
exhibitions.description: Five years of photographing the coastline from northern France to the southern Netherlands: Vanfleteren's sea shifts room by room from glassy calm through misty drift to storm.

exhibitions.title: Atlantic Window IV: Sedrig Verwoert
exhibitions.description: Choreographer Sedrig Verwoert traces dance in the diaspora, pairing a travelogue of his research into Winti, Kawina and Tambu in Suriname and Curacao with the dance film Strange Fruit 2.0.

exhibitions.title: Plantation along the Canal: Stories of People and Power
exhibitions.description: Explores how two of the house's 18th-century residents built their wealth on plantation trade, with an audio tour guided by a descendant of an enslaved woman from Suriname's Jagtlust plantation.

exhibitions.title: Plantation along the Canal
exhibitions.description: Stories of people and power: how Amsterdam's grand canal houses were financed through colonial trade and plantation slavery, told through residents and descendants of the enslaved.

exhibitions.title: The Art of Transformation
exhibitions.description: A theatre-history show on crossdressing, the Slingelandt theatre and revue star Louisette, exploring how costume and staging reshape identity.

exhibitions.title: Recent Additions to the Collection in the Art Gallery
exhibitions.venue: Joods Museum (Jewish Museum, Jewish Cultural Quarter)
exhibitions.description: Five years of acquisitions in the Art Gallery, from contemporary art to objects of Jewish firms and societies and personal mementoes of Holocaust victims.

exhibitions.title: Post/No/Bills #7 — Kexin Hao: Anatomy of Obstruction
exhibitions.description: Kexin Hao turns the corridor around the historic staircase into a body, with large anatomical drawings that read institutions as organisms, from lungs to kidney stones.

exhibitions.title: Disco
exhibitions.description: A tribute to disco's roots in Black, Latino and queer underground clubs, with tracks, videos, art, fashion and design celebrating freedom.

exhibitions.title: Mire Lee: Vomit My Blessing
exhibitions.description: South Korean artist Mire Lee installs a moving, almost-living structure of silicone, steel, motors and liquids exploring desire, decay and transformation.

exhibitions.title: Common Practice — Collaborations in Art and Design
exhibitions.description: The Stedelijk's biennial group show, this edition on collectives such as Hackers & Designers and Image Acts, from artworks and social design to manifestos and printed matter.

exhibitions.title: White Plays Black: Blackface on the Dutch Stage
exhibitions.description: How Dutch theatre normalised blackface, from medieval 'Moors' and 1840s minstrel shows to Zwarte Piet, told through the theatre collection with work by Kara Walker and Brian Elstak.

exhibitions.title: Rembrandts Craftsmanship
exhibitions.description: Five hands-on 'masterclasses' in Rembrandt's technique and tactics, with his etchings, paintings and a drawing, ending in a slow-looking room with The Anatomy Lesson of Jan Deijman.

exhibitions.title: Eva Gonzalès. A New Perspective
exhibitions.description: The first ever retrospective of French artist Eva Gonzalès (1847–1883), gathering her delicate paintings and pastels from international museums and private collections.

exhibitions.title: Drawing!
exhibitions.description: Over 100 drawings from European and American collections chart the revolution in drawing around 1600 led by Hendrick Goltzius, Jacques de Gheyn II and Abraham Bloemaert.

exhibitions.title: August Sander
exhibitions.description: A spring 2027 exhibition of the German photographer August Sander, known for his portraits of Weimar-era society; the museum will publish full details later.

exhibitions.title: Stathis Logothetis: Earth to Earth
exhibitions.venue: EMST National Museum of Contemporary Art
exhibitions.description: Retrospective of painter Stathis Logothetis (1925-1997): about 70 works and unpublished archive material, his first retrospective since 1994.
exhibitions.venue_address: Kallirrois Ave. & Amvr. Frantzi Str. (Former FIX Factory), 117 43 Athens, Greece

exhibitions.title: Jani Christou: Enantiodromia
exhibitions.venue: EMST National Museum of Contemporary Art
exhibitions.description: First major museum show on composer Jani Christou (1926-1970), drawn from his archive, shown to the public for the first time.
exhibitions.venue_address: Kallirrois Ave. & Amvr. Frantzi Str. (Former FIX Factory), 117 43 Athens, Greece

exhibitions.title: William Kentridge: Imitate the Sleep of Stones
exhibitions.description: The museum's first solo Kentridge show sets his Orpheus and Eurydice works among kouroi, sphinxes and funerary antiquities.

exhibitions.title: Pylos of Nestor: A Mycenaean Kingdom Revealed
exhibitions.description: 214 objects from Messenia trace a Mycenaean power centre and the Palace of Nestor at Ano Englianos, with excavation diaries and archival photographs.

exhibitions.title: An Ode to Things. Niki Kanagini. Retrospective
exhibitions.venue: EMST National Museum of Contemporary Art
exhibitions.description: Retrospective of Greek artist Niki Kanagini (1933-2008), from tapestries to participatory installations, with works from a promised family gift.
exhibitions.venue_address: Kallirrois Ave. & Amvr. Frantzi Str. (Former FIX Factory), 117 43 Athens, Greece

exhibitions.title: The Cult of Beauty
exhibitions.venue: CCCB – Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: How ideals of beauty were built, from Antiquity to the cosmetics industry, and a case for the bodies they leave out. Adapted from a Wellcome Collection show.

exhibitions.title: Sim Acquisition, Drawing and War
exhibitions.description: Nearly 100 newly acquired drawings by José Luis Rey Vila (Sim), a key visual chronicler of the Spanish Civil War: quick pencil and charcoal sketches of soldiers, bombings and civilians.
exhibitions.venue_address: Palau Nacional, Parc de Montjuïc, Barcelona

exhibitions.title: 50 anys dels concerts de la Transició. Barcelona, Palau d'Esports
exhibitions.description: Fifty years on from the 1975-76 Palau d'Esports recitals by Raimon, Lluís Llach and Pi de la Serra, told through photographs, period material and concert footage.

exhibitions.title: Visibles
exhibitions.description: Women in rural and farming Catalonia, through Llerona farmer Rosa Pruna i Esteve and four decades of rights won since the EU's 1986 directive on self-employed women.

exhibitions.title: Archive Drops: "We are the Shipyards"
exhibitions.description: A small display of documents about the Royal Shipyards from the museum's archive, with Braille and audio-described material.
exhibitions.venue_address: Avinguda de les Drassanes, s/n, 08001 Barcelona, Spain

exhibitions.title: Premis Enjoia't 2026
exhibitions.venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
exhibitions.description: 30 pieces from the 29th Enjoia't Contemporary Jewellery Awards organised by A-FAD: 15 professional and 15 student works by makers from more than ten countries.
exhibitions.venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Extramural project. Dora García
exhibitions.description: The museum's third Extramural edition: artist Dora García stages performances and interventions around Barcelona, treating the city as a space for critical thought.

exhibitions.title: (Un)ravelling trajectories
exhibitions.description: University of Barcelona Fine Arts alumni from the 'Cicle de Retorn' project in dialogue with alumni in the Suñol Soler Collection, including Ignasi Aballí and Susana Solano.
exhibitions.venue_address: Carrer de Mejía Lequerica 14, 08028 Barcelona, Spain

exhibitions.title: World Press Photo 2026
exhibitions.venue: CCCB – Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: The world's best-known photojournalism show returns: all 2026 World Press Photo winning images and multimedia projects from 42 photographers across six world regions.

exhibitions.title: Mater is the ultimate punk: The Analogue Rhizome
exhibitions.venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
exhibitions.description: A MATERFAD pop-up of eight fashion collections by Bau master's students, mixing biomaterials, 3D printing, light and craft to rethink fashion and nature.
exhibitions.venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Wounded Militiaman: The Recovery of an Irredeemable Painting
exhibitions.description: Francisco Mateos's Civil War propaganda painting, irreversibly deteriorated, is shown alongside AI-generated imagery that recovers its original visual impact.
exhibitions.venue_address: Palau Nacional, Parc de Montjuïc, Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Una fuerza del pasado
exhibitions.description: Works mainly from the "la Caixa" contemporary art collection that confront art history and tradition, titled after a Pasolini poem.
exhibitions.venue_address: Av. de Francesc Ferrer i Guàrdia, 6-8, 08038 Barcelona, Spain

exhibitions.title: Gaudí-Miró-Gomis: Deconstructed
exhibitions.description: Miró sculptures and prints and Joaquim Gomis's Gaudí photographs meet Tomorrow Bureau's AI, 3D-scan and animation installations. With the Fundació Joan Miró.

exhibitions.title: Invisible Animals
exhibitions.venue: Museu Blau – Museu de Ciències Naturals de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: Myth, life, extinction, de-extinction: animals we rarely see, from legendary beasts and extinct species to little-known living ones vital to healthy ecosystems.
exhibitions.venue_address: Plaça Leonardo da Vinci, 4-5, Parc del Fòrum, 08019 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Barcelona School of Architecture in shaping everyday life in the city (1875–2025)
exhibitions.description: Works and writings by ETSAB faculty trace how architecture, planning and landscape shaped daily life in Barcelona, with a focus on the sea.
exhibitions.venue_address: Avinguda de les Drassanes, s/n, 08001 Barcelona, Spain

exhibitions.title: KBr Flama'26
exhibitions.description: Sixth edition of KBr's showcase of emerging photographers from Barcelona's schools: Sara Bravo, Elena Bulet i Llopis, Meghan Mathews and Luca Gaetano Pira.
exhibitions.venue_address: Torre Mapfre, Avinguda del Litoral 30, 08005 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Anna Moreno. The Third Twist
exhibitions.venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: Recent works by Anna Moreno on utopian architecture, centred on The Terminal Beach, a road-movie film about Ricardo Bofill's unfinished 1979 settlement in the Algerian Sahara.

exhibitions.title: Dana Lixenberg. American Images
exhibitions.description: Retrospective of Dana Lixenberg's three decades of large-format portraits in the US, from Tupac and Biggie to Imperial Courts in Los Angeles and Shishmaref, Alaska.
exhibitions.venue_address: Torre Mapfre, Avinguda del Litoral 30, 08005 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Basel Abbas and Ruanne Abou-Rahme. Prisoners of Love: Until the Sun of Freedom
exhibitions.venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: First exhibition in Spain by Palestinian duo Basel Abbas and Ruanne Abou-Rahme, centred on their audiovisual installation Prisoners of Love and its layered stories of resistance.

exhibitions.title: Spiral of Time – Plaça dels Àngels – MACBA
exhibitions.venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: Edwin van der Heide's site-specific sound work, recording the ambient sounds of Plaça dels Àngels since July 2024 and playing them back as a shifting sonic portrait of the square.

exhibitions.title: Divided
exhibitions.description: London artist and publisher Camilla Wills (Divided Publishing) takes over the foyer, part of the Espai 13 season from 6:12 pm to 5:48 pm.

exhibitions.title: The Secret Life of Plants. Anselm Kiefer in the Grothe Collection
exhibitions.description: Barcelona's first major Anselm Kiefer show: around forty paintings, sculptures, installations, photographs and artist's books, mostly from Hans Grothe's collection, on memory, matter and knowledge.

exhibitions.title: Instrumental Baschet. La utopia ressonant
exhibitions.venue: Museu de la Música de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: The sound sculptures of Bernard and François Baschet, 1950s inventors who built electricity-free instruments from steel, aluminium, cardboard and inflatable cushions.
exhibitions.venue_address: L'Auditori, Carrer de Lepant 150 (2nd floor), 08013 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Opening the Archive 08. Le gros orteil.
exhibitions.description: Miró's newly donated drawing Untitled (1930) shown with his sketches for the series, likely inspired by Georges Bataille's essay 'Le Gros Orteil'.

exhibitions.title: Pau Casals a Puerto Rico
exhibitions.venue: Museu de la Música de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: For Casals' 150th anniversary, the first show of the archive from his last 18 years in Puerto Rico (1955–73), founding institutions, conducting and composing.
exhibitions.venue_address: L'Auditori, Carrer de Lepant 150 (2nd floor), 08013 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Music for a problem
exhibitions.venue: Museu de la Música de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: Installation by Gerard Valverde Ros and Marc Villanueva: a magnetic instrument for remixing recordings of Barcelona's 1989 Contemporary Music Week.
exhibitions.venue_address: L'Auditori, Carrer de Lepant 150 (2nd floor), 08013 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Charlotte Perriand. Free to Rethink the World
exhibitions.description: Spain's first exhibition on Charlotte Perriand, the pioneering modernist designer from Le Corbusier's atelier and a lifelong friend of Sert and Miró.

exhibitions.title: André Ricard. Disseny en ús
exhibitions.venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
exhibitions.description: A survey of André Ricard, a pioneer of contemporary Catalan design, focused on everyday objects conceived as tools serving people and society.
exhibitions.venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Asunción Bastida
exhibitions.venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
exhibitions.description: Rediscovers Asunción Bastida (1902-1995), the Barcelona couturier who was the only woman in the top circle of Spanish haute couture, showing collections from Madrid to New York.
exhibitions.venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: A Journey Through Time at the Royal Shipyards of Barcelona
exhibitions.description: The story of the Drassanes Reials from their 13th-century origins under Peter III to today: the world's largest surviving medieval shipyards.
exhibitions.venue_address: Avinguda de les Drassanes, s/n, 08001 Barcelona, Spain

exhibitions.title: Aurèlia Muñoz. Beings
exhibitions.venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: A full survey of textile artist Aurèlia Muñoz, from early collages and embroideries to unseen large macramé structures, her iconic kite-sculptures and late handmade-paper installations.

exhibitions.title: Pere Portabella: The Committed Gaze
exhibitions.venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: Screenings of Pere Portabella's films from the MACBA Collection for his centenary: radical cinema made under censorship that rejects linear narrative and treats form as a political stance.

exhibitions.title: Echoes: Videos from the Han Nefkens Foundation Donation
exhibitions.venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: Collection display of videos by artists from around the world, donated by the Han Nefkens Foundation, where documentary and poetic moving images are shaped by texture, sound and materiality.

exhibitions.title: Counter-Information: Video-Nou / Servei de Vídeo Comunitari
exhibitions.venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: Collection display tracing Video-Nou and the Servei de Vídeo Comunitari, a collective that used video as a tool of political counter-information in Catalonia from 1977 to 1983.

exhibitions.title: Tiburones. Los guardianes del océano
exhibitions.description: Australian Museum show on 450 million years of sharks: ten life-size models from great white to Helicoprion, a megalodon jaw to touch, interactives and an oceanarium.

exhibitions.title: Aurèlia Muñoz. El tèxtil com a pretext
exhibitions.venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
exhibitions.description: For the Aurèlia Muñoz Year, three early textile works from the collection: the 1961 tapestry La Barcelona gòtica and two 1962 screen-printed jute table covers.
exhibitions.venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: The Reverse Journey. A Sound Fresco through Romanesque Art
exhibitions.description: Ona Balló's sound installation in the Romanesque galleries, playing recordings from six Pyrenean churches whose apse murals now hang in the museum.
exhibitions.venue_address: Palau Nacional, Parc de Montjuïc, Barcelona

exhibitions.title: LED LIGHT
exhibitions.description: Barcelona artist Victor Ruiz Colomer closes the Espai 13 season with work driven by thermodynamics and how Sert's building shapes movement through it.

exhibitions.title: Soy Asurbanipal, rey del mundo, rey de Asiria
exhibitions.description: Assyrian treasures from the British Museum trace the life of Ashurbanipal (669-631 BC): warrior, scholar, lion hunter and builder of a great library.
exhibitions.venue_address: Av. de Francesc Ferrer i Guàrdia, 6-8, 08038 Barcelona, Spain

exhibitions.title: La Cuina de Frankfurt (1926 – 2026). Disseny i gènere a l'espai domèstic
exhibitions.venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
exhibitions.description: For its centenary, Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky's 1926 Frankfurt Kitchen and how industrial design reshaped housework, women's roles and the modern home.
exhibitions.venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Picasso and architecture
exhibitions.description: How Picasso's cubist space shaped modern architecture, from Guernica's 1937 pavilion and his Barcelona architects' college friezes to his influence on Le Corbusier.

exhibitions.title: Vectors. Art digital per pensar el futur
exhibitions.venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
exhibitions.description: A survey of contemporary digital art by artists working with computational technologies, from generative art and live creation to critiques of the invisible infrastructure of the digital world.
exhibitions.venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

exhibitions.title: The Atomic Age
exhibitions.venue: CCCB – Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona
exhibitions.description: 20th- and 21st-century art responding to the atom and the bomb, from early physics and mysticism to nuclear protest. Adapted from the Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris show.

exhibitions.title: «Així és la guerra...». Diaris personals de combatents (1936-1939)
exhibitions.description: The Spanish Civil War through combatants' personal diaries: fears, routines, drawings, poems and songs, with the notebooks treated as an exceptional historical source.

exhibitions.title: Jujol, by Perejaume
exhibitions.description: The MNAC's first major Josep Maria Jujol show, curated by artist Perejaume from the architect's newly donated archive, with works by Gaudí, Taut, Tatlin and Matisse.
exhibitions.venue_address: Palau Nacional, Parc de Montjuïc, Barcelona

exhibitions.title: Penny Siopis. Ink, blood and history
exhibitions.description: South African artist Penny Siopis links personal and collective memory, apartheid and colonial repression across painting, drawing and film.

exhibitions.title: Tàpies, Portabella: Politics of Friendship
exhibitions.description: For Pere Portabella's centenary: his lifelong friendship with Tàpies, from the early Franco years on, as a model of alliances between art and politics.

exhibitions.title: Cristina Lucas. E-conmotion
exhibitions.description: Cristina Lucas traces four industrial revolutions, from coal to AI, as battlegrounds of power and colonialism, with triptychs made from each era's materials.

exhibitions.title: Being Related: Shared Language, Shared Knowledge?
exhibitions.description: Video installation on endangered languages and family, with community members documenting their languages, made with the Endangered Languages Archive.

exhibitions.title: A Country in a Container – The Disposal of East German State Symbols
exhibitions.description: What became of the GDR's flags, emblems and medals after 1990: dumped in containers, sold at flea markets, and still shaping how Germany remembers.

exhibitions.title: Helmut Newton's One-off Album
exhibitions.description: A unique album Newton assembled in 1999 for collector Gert Elfering, shown in Berlin for the first time: hand-annotated small prints, Polaroids and outtakes.

exhibitions.title: Scandal! Hermione von Preuschen and the “Mors Imperator”
exhibitions.description: The painter, writer and traveller whose 1887 painting Mors Imperator, rejected by the Berlin Academy of Arts, made her famous overnight.

exhibitions.title: Rooms / Stages
exhibitions.description: Helmut Newton Foundation group show on space as stage: a dozen artists' rooms, sets and deserted interiors beside Newton's hotel-suite fashion shoots and murals.

exhibitions.title: Between the Lines: Daniel Libeskind and the Jewish Museum Berlin
exhibitions.description: For the building's 25th anniversary, drawings and models trace how Libeskind's 1989 competition design became one of the most influential museum buildings. Free.

exhibitions.title: 3hd 2026: Beyond Imagining
exhibitions.description: A video programme by Creamcake exploring how the real and the invented bleed into each other, with work from four artists on power, identity and institutional critique.

exhibitions.title: Manatunga: Artistic Interventions by George Nuku
exhibitions.description: Three large interventions by Māori artist George Nuku in two rooms of the Oceania galleries, made in polystyrene and Plexiglas during his Collaborative Museum fellowships.

exhibitions.title: Gabriele Stötzer: Dabei sein und nicht schweigen
exhibitions.description: The largest institutional solo show yet of East German artist Gabriele Stötzer: about 150 works in painting, photography, textile, Super 8 film and performance on justice, gender and resistance.

exhibitions.title: Friends for the Arts of East Asia in Berlin
exhibitions.description: Marks 100 years of the Society for East Asian Art with museum holdings and loans, including an 18th-century Japanese Buddhist painting.

exhibitions.title: 100 Years of the Dictionary of the Egyptian Language
exhibitions.description: In the Mythological Hall, a centenary show on the Egyptian Dictionary, begun in this building in 1897 from over a million hand-copied index cards.
exhibitions.venue_address: Bodestraße, 10178 Berlin (visitor entrance via the James-Simon-Galerie)

exhibitions.title: Digital Sovereignty Experience Space
exhibitions.description: Free, hands-on space by the MobilitätDigital initiative in Hall 6 of the Ladestraße: VR accident replays, AI avatars and an image-recognition challenge on data and AI in mobility.

exhibitions.title: The Portrait of the German Chancellor: First Unveiling of the Official Portrait of Former Chancellor Angela Merkel
exhibitions.description: Jérémie Queyras's official portrait of Angela Merkel, Chancellor for 16 years, on public display for the first time before it joins the Chancellery's gallery.
exhibitions.venue_address: Am Kupfergraben (entrance via Monbijoubrücke), 10178 Berlin, Germany

exhibitions.title: Courage: Sisters in Spirit
exhibitions.description: The Prater Galerie's reopening show: eight women artists, pairing GDR-era collection works by Jetelová, Vent and Schulze Eldowy with contemporaries from Eastern Europe.

exhibitions.title: Ruin and Rush. Berlin 1910–1930
exhibitions.description: Around 35 collection works by Dix, Höch and others on Berlin between war, excess, poverty and emancipation in the 1910s and 1920s.

exhibitions.title: Shilpa Gupta: What Still Holds
exhibitions.description: Works by Shilpa Gupta on language, borders and power, in direct dialogue with Joseph Beuys and the Marx Collection.

exhibitions.title: Rafik Greiss: The City and the City
exhibitions.description: Rafik Greiss's first institutional solo show premieres a new film essay drifting through Cairo, Alexandria and the Western Desert on time, memory and history.

exhibitions.title: CHANEL Commission: Lina Lapelytė. We Make Years Out of Hours
exhibitions.description: Lina Lapelytė turns the Historic Hall into a polyphonic stage for a participatory choreography.

exhibitions.title: Susan Hiller: Bad Dreams
exhibitions.description: The first Berlin survey of Susan Hiller, a pioneer of conceptual and video art, with hypnotic audiovisual installations probing fantasy, fear and the unconscious.

exhibitions.title: Daniel Chodowiecki, 1726–1801. Images of the Enlightenment in Berlin
exhibitions.description: A cabinet show marking the 300th birthday of Chodowiecki, star of late-18th-century Berlin, with 20+ of his key works on the Enlightenment's social questions.

exhibitions.title: KOO JEONG A: OUSSSEAN
exhibitions.description: KOO JEONG A's first major solo show in Germany: multisensory environments of light, scent, sound and temperature, reconfigured for KW's architecture.

exhibitions.title: Destiny in the Stars: The Beginnings of the Zodiac
exhibitions.description: The history of the zodiac from Babylonia to Egypt and the Greco-Roman world, from star tablets to celestial ceilings.
exhibitions.venue_address: Bodestraße, 10178 Berlin (visitor entrance via the James-Simon-Galerie)

exhibitions.title: Founded on Antiquity: Berlin's First Museum
exhibitions.description: The upper-floor show revisits the museum's 1830 beginnings, reuniting antiquities from its first display around a large model of Schinkel's original building.

exhibitions.title: The Opposite of Now
exhibitions.description: Twelve contemporary art projects, by Yael Bartana, William Forsythe, Alexander Kluge and others, imagine paths to a different present. Old Building, level 1.

exhibitions.title: Lauren Greenfield: Social Studies
exhibitions.description: Lauren Greenfield's social experiment on growing up in the digital age: teenagers, selfies and the pressures of social media.

exhibitions.title: Miji Ih: Mouths: On Water and Whisky
exhibitions.description: Miji Ih's largest solo show: photography, archive material, sound and video on "comfort women" and the lives of women around US military bases in Japan, South Korea and Germany.

exhibitions.title: InterNationalgalerie 1: National Museum in Warsaw
exhibitions.description: The National Museum in Warsaw opens a new guest series with “Inventing Myths”, showing Polish masters such as Malczewski and Matejko on the first floor.

exhibitions.title: Nature and German History. Faith – Biology – Power
exhibitions.description: Eight centuries of how Germans defined and politicised 'nature', from medieval faith through Nazi ideas of natural law to 20th-century environmental and anti-nuclear movements.
exhibitions.venue_address: Unter den Linden 2, 10117 Berlin (entrance: Hinter dem Gießhaus 3)

exhibitions.title: Sofie Dawo. Textile Experiments
exhibitions.description: 22 textile works by Sofie Dawo (1926–2010), who reworked fabric by disrupting and damaging it, creating objects that sit between art and craft.

exhibitions.title: Kreuzberg: Kunst und Migration seit 1960
exhibitions.description: Around 130 works on labour migration, exile, housing, racism and solidarity in Kreuzberg since the 'guest worker' era, from rarely shown historical pieces to new commissions.

exhibitions.title: Christoph Schlingensief: Es ist nicht mehr mein Problem, macht eure Scheiße alleine
exhibitions.description: Schlingensief's first comprehensive Berlin exhibition in over a decade, from political actions to radical stage productions and performance art, focused on questioning, doubt and failure.

exhibitions.title: Susanne Kriemann: In the Sun's Fever Flutter Butterflies in the Stomach
exhibitions.description: After Nature Prize 26: Berlin artist Susanne Kriemann traces the atomic age's remnants at former uranium mines, using autoradiography in her Pechblende (Fever) series.

exhibitions.title: Stelios Kallinikou: Cliffs Among Dreams
exhibitions.description: After Nature Prize 26: photographs, films and sculptural assemblages from Akrotiri, Cyprus, where rich ecosystems meet military infrastructure.

exhibitions.title: Lovis Corinth. Then came Berlin!
exhibitions.description: Major show on Lovis Corinth's rise in Berlin after 1900: his expressive painting, his women's painting school, his theatre work and his domestic circle.

exhibitions.title: Rubens, Jordaens, van Dyck. Flemish Master Drawings
exhibitions.description: More than 100 Flemish drawings from 1570 to 1650 by 28 artists, many shown for the first time in fifty years.

exhibitions.title: The Holocaust – What Did the Germans Know?
exhibitions.description: Around 300 objects in three parts (propaganda, everyday clues and pieced-together knowledge) ask what ordinary Germans knew about the Holocaust.

exhibitions.title: Josef Kaiser. Building for the GDR
exhibitions.description: Drawings, photographs, films and models on the GDR architect behind Karl-Marx-Allee's Kino International, with new works by three contemporary artists.

exhibitions.title: Carrie Mae Weems: The Heart of the Matter
exhibitions.description: Four-decade retrospective of Carrie Mae Weems: over 100 photographs and videos, from the Kitchen Table Series and Family Pictures and Stories to her new Preach series.

exhibitions.title: Thomas Billhardt: Die Augen weit offen
exhibitions.description: Key series from 1959 to 1972 by the late Berlin photojournalist, from Alexanderplatz and FDJ events to Vietnam and Cuba.

exhibitions.title: Mirae kh Rhee: Hand-Me-Down
exhibitions.description: Mirae kh Rhee asks how objects reached their places in collections and who collects and why, in a cabinet-of-curiosities project from a transnational feminist, decolonial view.

exhibitions.title: Banz & Bowinkel: COMPOSITIONS / DRIFT
exhibitions.description: Computer-generated forms drift and collide on the museum's LED façade. Best seen after dark from the street opposite the entrance.

exhibitions.title: Paperwork – Jumping He. Blackbox #18
exhibitions.description: Posters, books, graphic works and paper installations from more than 25 years of practice by graphic designer Jumping He. Free public tours on Sundays at 15:00.

exhibitions.title: 2101 – Future Ceramics: Dining Culture of the Future
exhibitions.description: Berlin University of the Arts students imagine the tableware of 2101, shown alongside historical porcelain and faience from the museum's collection.

exhibitions.title: Across Epochs: Gursky, Lucas, Miró, Warhol and the Art of the Long 19th Century
exhibitions.description: For the 150th anniversary, 20th- and 21st-century works from the Nationalgalerie collection are set beside 19th-century art on all three floors.

exhibitions.title: Maurizio Cattelan. NIGHT – Preis der Nationalgalerie 2026
exhibitions.description: Cattelan's first major solo show in Germany, for the 2026 Preis der Nationalgalerie: Him, Novecento and new commissions in Mies's glass hall.

exhibitions.title: Conservation in Dialogue
exhibitions.description: A look at the hidden work of museum conservators, through restored objects such as Canadian crest poles, a Qing lacquer cabinet and a Mongolian shrine.

exhibitions.title: [ materialistin ]: Matter of Care, Care of Matter
exhibitions.description: Group exhibition by the artists' collective [ materialistin ], highlighting new forms of collective practice and solidarity.

exhibitions.title: Dioscuri – The Given Day
exhibitions.description: Artist Michael Müller reworks the myth of the twins Castor and Polydeuces in the staircase hall, a meditation on time and mortality.
exhibitions.venue_address: Bodestraße, 10178 Berlin (visitor entrance via the James-Simon-Galerie)

exhibitions.title: Portraits! Surprising Encounters from Botticelli to Lempicka
exhibitions.description: Around 80 portraits spanning five centuries, from rulers in full glory to intimate scenes of friendship and proud self-portraits, Botticelli to Lempicka.

exhibitions.title: Roger Ballen: roger ballen.! drawing meets photography
exhibitions.description: Roger Ballen's path from black-and-white photography to mixed media and Art Brut, with Polaroids, etchings, drawings and a new Drawing Man installation.

exhibitions.title: Cesar Klein. Image Space Stage
exhibitions.description: Berlin's first monographic show on Cesar Klein, 150 years after his birth: Neue Secession co-founder, painter, and a leading stage and interior designer of the 1920s.

exhibitions.title: Escaping the Tumultuous World on Tranquil Rivers
exhibitions.description: Marks 120 years of the East Asian Art Collection with the fisherman motif in Chinese painting, a symbol of escape from a turbulent world.

exhibitions.title: fuga: Sound Exhibition by Netta Weiser
exhibitions.description: Netta Weiser's first sound exhibition in Berlin, in the Listening Space: 1930s wax cylinder recordings from Siwa, Egypt, by Brigitte Schiffer, reworked through a queer-diasporic lens.

exhibitions.title: Extreme Tension. Art between Politics and Society (1945–2000)
exhibitions.description: The Nationalgalerie's post-war collection from East and West, 1945–2000, including Barnett Newman's Who's Afraid of Red, Yellow and Blue IV.

exhibitions.title: Jeewi Lee. Residual Memories. GASAG Art Prize 2026
exhibitions.description: The GASAG Art Prize winner's first institutional solo show in Berlin: paintings, sculptures and installations built from sand and traces of time.

exhibitions.title: Controversial Kinship. Colonial and National Socialist Violence
exhibitions.description: A comparative exhibition on colonial and Nazi violence in the 20th century: racism, forced labour and concentration camps, and how the two regimes resemble and differ.
exhibitions.venue_address: Unter den Linden 2, 10117 Berlin (entrance: Hinter dem Gießhaus 3)

exhibitions.title: Christoph Schlingensief. Deutschlandsuche ’99
exhibitions.description: A room devoted to Christoph Schlingensief, centred on Deutschland versenken (1999), his action of 'sinking Germany' in New York.

exhibitions.title: Histories of Tanzania
exhibitions.description: Over 10,000 Tanzanian objects from the Ethnologisches Museum shown alongside Tanzanian curators' and artists' perspectives on German and British colonial rule.

exhibitions.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: seeing sound, hearing time
exhibitions.description: The first major European retrospective of Ryuichi Sakamoto: seven works in five large-scale installations, opening during Berlin Art Week.

exhibitions.title: SuperCity 3000. Our City of the Future
exhibitions.description: An exhibition by children for children: models built by 60 young 'future curators' from four Berlin schools imagine a liveable city of tomorrow, with hands-on stations in the Ladestraße.

exhibitions.title: Next Door
exhibitions.description: Group show in the Rieckhallen with Tacita Dean and Bruce Nauman, Thomas Demand, Olafur Eliasson, Henrik Håkansson and Tomás Saraceno, on view until further notice.

exhibitions.title: ZUGvögel – Collection in Motion
exhibitions.description: Around 11,500 historic mounted birds, moved out of the Historic Bird Hall during its restoration, tell stories of bird diversity, war, research and conservation.

exhibitions.title: If I Were King or Queen…
exhibitions.description: Young Visions from Neukölln: eleven young people on today's injustices and a fairer future. Visitors can take a seat on the throne. In BERLIN GLOBAL.

exhibitions.title: Dara Tûyê – The Mulberry Tree
exhibitions.description: Feminist voices on war and gardens: art, photography and interviews on women's solidarity across borders and the healing power of community gardens.

exhibitions.title: The Crown of Kerch: Treasures from the Dawn of European History
exhibitions.description: Migration-period gold and garnet jewellery from the Diergardt collection, on loan from Cologne, led by a noblewoman's diadem from Crimea.
exhibitions.venue_address: Bodestraße, 10178 Berlin (visitor entrance via the James-Simon-Galerie)

exhibitions.title: On Water: WasserWissen in Berlin
exhibitions.description: Free show in the Humboldt Lab pairing Berlin University Alliance water research with artistic takes on water and the climate crisis.

exhibitions.title: Pewter from the Middle Ages to Art Nouveau
exhibitions.description: Some 100 pewter works at Schloss Köpenick trace the material from sacred objects to everyday items, including furniture by cabinetmaker Johann Daniel Sommer combining tortoiseshell, horn and pewter.

exhibitions.title: Objects. History. Stories. Reviewing the Collection
exhibitions.description: Around 200 objects from the DHM's million-piece collection, some never shown before, exploring provenance, 150 years of collecting and how places have shaped history.
exhibitions.venue_address: Unter den Linden 2, 10117 Berlin (entrance: Hinter dem Gießhaus 3)

exhibitions.title: DINOSAURS! – Age of the Giant Lizards
exhibitions.description: Original fossils from the Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous, from early Plateosaurus to the superbly preserved T. rex Tristan Otto, with an Allosaurus skull.

exhibitions.title: Intermezzo: Revisiting Helmut Newton
exhibitions.description: An immersive four-screen film on Helmut Newton with unseen footage and interviews, plus a wall of nearly 100 exhibition posters, before a new permanent display in 2027.

exhibitions.title: Time Travel in the Old Tiergarten District
exhibitions.description: Free Kunstbibliothek presentation on the artistic community around Matthäikirchplatz a century ago, whose cultural life ended in 1933.

exhibitions.title: Swedish Modernism
exhibitions.description: Germany's first comprehensive survey of Swedish modernism: Sigrid Hjertén, Isaac Grünewald, Nils Dardel and the Göteborg Colourists, on loan from Moderna Museet, Stockholm.

exhibitions.title: Sophie Calle: Is It Better?
exhibitions.description: Sophie Calle combines works made in Berlin with others that reference the museum's history as a railway station.

exhibitions.title: Klaus Hack
exhibitions.description: Wood sculpture, reliefs, woodcuts and drawings by Klaus Hack (b. 1966), whose carved figures sit between surreal creatures and structural forms. Public opening Sunday 15 November 2026.

exhibitions.title: Sound Bodies – Variations on a Theme of Art
exhibitions.description: A musical intervention pairing historical and modern instruments with artworks that depict music, from late antique textiles and angel choirs to Canova's 'Dancer'.
exhibitions.venue_address: Am Kupfergraben (entrance via Monbijoubrücke), 10178 Berlin, Germany

exhibitions.title: "BIZARRE". The History of the Strangest Word in the World
exhibitions.description: Traces the word "bizarre" from the Renaissance to 21st-century imagery, with works from the Kunstbibliothek, Gemäldegalerie and Kupferstichkabinett.

exhibitions.title: Tracing Shiva. Between Berlin and Kathmandu
exhibitions.description: A film and research project by Deepak Tolange on the copper-gilded Chaturmukh Shiva Linga kosh in Berlin's Asian art collection and the loss of Nepal's cultural assets.

exhibitions.title: Agua. The Art and Cosmologies of Water
exhibitions.description: Twenty artworks from Brazil, Colombia and Chile show water as a source of knowledge and spirituality and as a ground of environmental conflict, made with Indigenous and traditional communities.

exhibitions.title: Ulay, Ulay & Abramović
exhibitions.description: Ulay's early photography, S'he and FOTOTOT, and his 1976 theft of Spitzweg's The Poor Poet from this museum, plus his 1976–88 collaboration with Marina Abramović.

exhibitions.title: Helmut Newton. White Women / Sleepless Nights / Big Nudes
exhibitions.description: Over 200 photographs from Newton's three landmark books of 1976–81, with original maquettes and prints, marking 50 years of White Women.

exhibitions.title: Unsere Münzen! Gedenkprägungen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland (2006–2026)
exhibitions.description: The Münzkabinett shows 20 years of German commemorative coins across 200+ themes and asks who decides what our money looks like. Page in German only.
exhibitions.venue_address: Am Kupfergraben (entrance via Monbijoubrücke), 10178 Berlin, Germany

exhibitions.title: Echt Foto! Photography between Paper and Pixel
exhibitions.description: The Kunstbibliothek traces a material history of photography, from glass and paper to screens and AI, through the varied objects of its Photography Collection.

exhibitions.title: BPA// Exhibition 2026
exhibitions.description: New work by ten emerging artists from the BPA// Berlin program for artists, the mentoring scheme founded by Angela Bulloch, Simon Denny and Willem de Rooij.

exhibitions.title: Schatten Reich. The Other German Art 1933–1945
exhibitions.description: Non-representational art made under National Socialism by Willi Baumeister, Jeanne Mammen, Alexej von Jawlensky and others.

exhibitions.title: Amin Yousefi: Defensive Readiness: Revised Version
exhibitions.description: C/O Berlin Talent Award 2026 (Body Politics): Amin Yousefi's solo show combines photography, diagrammatic drawings and mapped gestures on how state control is enacted through the body.

exhibitions.title: Drag, Desire and the City. Rolf von Bergmann. Photographs
exhibitions.description: About 160 photographs of the queer, club and art scenes of 1970s–80s West Berlin and New York, from Klaus Nomi to Divine, by the little-known Rolf von Bergmann.

exhibitions.title: Swimming with Sharks: A Deep Dive into Shark Biology and Behavior
exhibitions.description: Jaws from Harvard's collections, underwater photography by Keith Ellenbogen and the science of shark skin recast the ocean's most misunderstood megafauna as more menaced than menacing.
exhibitions.venue_address: 26 Oxford Street, Cambridge, MA 02138, United States

exhibitions.title: Imagined Nation
exhibitions.description: For the USA's 250th, rare material from George Washington's own library (including his copy of Paine's Common Sense) alongside early Declaration printings and WWII posters. Rotates through 2026.
exhibitions.venue_address: 10½ Beacon Street, Boston, MA 02108, United States

exhibitions.title: List Projects 35: Pap Souleye Fall
exhibitions.description: In Pap Souleye Fall's practice, technological error is a space of refuge one can slip into, concealed from larger systems of control.
exhibitions.venue_address: Wiesner Building, 20 Ames Street, Bldg. E15-109, Atrium level, Cambridge, MA 02139, United States

exhibitions.title: Reality and Imagination: Rembrandt and the Jews in the Dutch Republic
exhibitions.description: Jews as patrons, collectors and subjects in 17th-century Amsterdam, where Rembrandt lived in the heart of the Jewish district and drew commissions from his neighbours.
exhibitions.venue_address: 465 Huntington Avenue, Boston, MA 02115, United States

exhibitions.title: Freezing Time: Edgerton and the Beauty of the Machine Age
exhibitions.description: Harold "Doc" Edgerton's stroboscope and high-speed flash photographs from the 1930s, freezing motion in factories and the natural world, reprinted from the original negatives.
exhibitions.venue_address: 314 Main Street, Gambrill Center (Building E28), Cambridge, MA 02142, USA

exhibitions.title: Declaring the Revolution: America's Printed Path to Independence
exhibitions.venue: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
exhibitions.description: Rare pamphlets, broadsides, maps and engravings from David M. Rubenstein's Americana collection trace how print carried the ideas behind the Declaration of Independence, marking its 250th anniversary.
exhibitions.venue_address: Columbia Point, Boston, MA 02125, United States

exhibitions.title: Maverick Kings: Three Visionary Pharaohs of Egypt's Golden Age
exhibitions.description: Hatshepsut, Akhenaten and Tutankhamun through the art of Egypt's 18th Dynasty (1550–1292 BCE), when royal patronage drove a wave of societal and artistic change. Ann and Graham Gund Gallery.
exhibitions.venue_address: 465 Huntington Avenue, Boston, MA 02115, United States

exhibitions.title: Where's Boston? 50 Years Later
exhibitions.description: Constantine Manos spent nine months in 1974 photographing Boston's streets for the Bicentennial. Fifty years on, the flea markets, protests and ball games return to the Calderwood Gallery.
exhibitions.venue_address: 10½ Beacon Street, Boston, MA 02108, United States

exhibitions.title: Constitutive Outside
exhibitions.venue: Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts
exhibitions.description: Markele Cullins, Jibade-Khalil Huffman, Steffani Jemison and Rindon Johnson use performance, installation and screen-based work to turn the gaze into a negotiation rather than a position of mastery.
exhibitions.venue_address: 24 Quincy Street, Cambridge, MA 02138, United States

exhibitions.title: Knowledge Is Myth: Chimeric Continuities
exhibitions.venue: Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts
exhibitions.description: Enzo Camacho and Ami Lien, Candice Lin, Cole Lu, and Ayoung Yu and Nicholas Oh treat mythmaking as a way of making and unmaking knowledge, drawing on pre-colonial, diasporic and chimeric traditions.
exhibitions.venue_address: 24 Quincy Street, Cambridge, MA 02138, United States

exhibitions.title: We The People: The Adamses & the U.S. Constitution
exhibitions.description: Documents and artifacts from the Adams Presidential Library trace how Americans moved from the weak Articles of Confederation through debates over state versus centralized power to a ratified U.S. Constitution.

exhibitions.title: 1776: Declaring Independence
exhibitions.description: Handwritten copies of the Declaration by John Adams and Thomas Jefferson, a rare Dunlap broadside, letters and diaries trace how the document grew from draft to founding text.

exhibitions.title: 40 Years of Contemporary Art
exhibitions.description: An anniversary display tracing the List's origins in the Hayden Gallery, founded 1950, and four decades in the Wiesner Building since it opened on 1 October 1985.
exhibitions.venue_address: Wiesner Building, 20 Ames Street, Bldg. E15-109, Atrium level, Cambridge, MA 02139, United States

exhibitions.title: To My Best Friend
exhibitions.description: More than 50 works Fotene Demoulas and Tom Cote helped bring into the ICA Collection, with Laura Owens, Njideka Akunyili Crosby, Olga de Amaral, Sarah Sze and Lorna Simpson.
exhibitions.venue_address: 25 Harbor Shore Drive, Boston, MA 02210, United States

exhibitions.title: The Road to Revolution: Massachusetts and the Independence Movement
exhibitions.description: Boston's flagship semiquincentennial show, made with the Massachusetts Historical Society and anchored by a rare 1776 Boston broadside of the Declaration of Independence.
exhibitions.venue_address: 206 Washington Street, Boston, MA 02109, United States

exhibitions.title: Introduction to the History of Art
exhibitions.description: A University Teaching Gallery installation asking what art is, why it matters, and by whom its history is written: objects chosen to be studied by Harvard students and open to all.
exhibitions.venue_address: 32 Quincy Street, Cambridge, MA 02138, United States

exhibitions.title: Split | Second
exhibitions.description: Instruments and artworks spanning 340 years across four sections - Earth Time, Mechanical Time, Electric Time, Atomic Time - tracing how precise timekeeping became a negotiated human construct.
exhibitions.venue_address: 314 Main Street, Gambrill Center (Building E28), Cambridge, MA 02142, USA

exhibitions.title: On Location: Drawing the Outdoors
exhibitions.description: A journey through drawings by groundbreaking 19th-century artists who left the studio to look outside for inspiration, showing how a close relationship with nature shaped artistic vision.
exhibitions.venue_address: 32 Quincy Street, Cambridge, MA 02138, United States

exhibitions.title: Leilah Babirye: Embaga ya Naki ne Naki (Wedding of Naki and Naki)
exhibitions.description: The Ugandan-born artist premieres new ceramic and wood sculptures staging a queer wedding, each figure cast as bride, groom or guest, watched over by charred-wood ancestors.
exhibitions.venue_address: 25 Harbor Shore Drive, Boston, MA 02210, United States

exhibitions.title: The Book of Esther in the Age of Rembrandt
exhibitions.description: Dutch paintings, tapestries, Persian textiles and Jewish ceremonial objects trace how the biblical heroine Esther became a shared symbol for Jewish and Protestant communities in the 1600s Netherlands.
exhibitions.venue_address: 25 Evans Way, Boston, MA 02115, United States

exhibitions.title: Cynthia Daignault: Valley
exhibitions.description: A new multi-panel installation by the Baltimore painter, whose "long-form painting" breaks Yosemite's Tunnel View into interrelated canvases. Paul and Catherine Buttenwieser Gallery.
exhibitions.venue_address: 25 Harbor Shore Drive, Boston, MA 02210, United States

exhibitions.title: Suzanne Jackson: What Is Love
exhibitions.description: Six decades of lyrical painting by Suzanne Jackson (b. 1944), shaped by a deep respect for the natural world and a belief in the interconnectedness of all living things.
exhibitions.venue_address: 465 Huntington Avenue, Boston, MA 02115, United States

exhibitions.title: Michal Rovner: Esther Scrolls
exhibitions.description: In the Fenway Gallery, Israeli video and installation artist Michal Rovner responds to the Book of Esther with her own scroll works, shown alongside the Museum's Rembrandt-era Esther exhibition.
exhibitions.venue_address: 25 Evans Way, Boston, MA 02115, United States

exhibitions.title: Picasso, Miró, Dalí: Unbound
exhibitions.description: The livre d'artiste as a revolution in book-making, seen through Picasso, Miró and Dalí: extravagant, experimental volumes that turned the printed page into an art form.
exhibitions.venue_address: 465 Huntington Avenue, Boston, MA 02115, United States

exhibitions.title: Sonder
exhibitions.description: Teen artists from the ICA's Teen Exhibitions Program explore sonder, the realization that every life is as complex as one's own. Teen Gallery, Seaport Studio.
exhibitions.venue_address: 25 Harbor Shore Drive, Boston, MA 02210, United States

exhibitions.title: Michal Rovner: Untitled/Night, 2016
exhibitions.description: A jackal with glowing eyes keeps watch from the Anne H. Fitzpatrick Facade, filmed with a night-vision camera near Rovner's home and evoking Anubis, guide of souls to the afterlife. Free to view outside.
exhibitions.venue_address: 25 Evans Way, Boston, MA 02115, United States

exhibitions.title: Crochet Coral Reef
exhibitions.description: Margaret Wertheim and mathematician Erik Demaine turn fibre art, hyperbolic geometry and marine science into collective climate action, highlighting the threat to coral reefs. Opens with the OCEANS season.
exhibitions.venue_address: 314 Main Street, Gambrill Center (Building E28), Cambridge, MA 02142, USA

exhibitions.title: Öyvind Fahlström: Are You Happy?
exhibitions.description: The Swedish-Brazilian artist's playful, politically barbed work from 1960s–70s America, built on his idea of art as "a fusion of 'pleasure' and 'insight'" and made to be handled by its audience.
exhibitions.venue_address: 465 Huntington Avenue, Boston, MA 02115, United States

exhibitions.title: Sensing Oceans
exhibitions.description: Immersive installations by Marshmallow Laser Feast set against 19th-century oceanographic equipment, exploring how we make sense of the earth's oceans. Opens with the OCEANS season at MIT Future Fest.
exhibitions.venue_address: 314 Main Street, Gambrill Center (Building E28), Cambridge, MA 02142, USA

exhibitions.title: Donna Ferrato: 'Living with the Enemy' and the Power of Women
exhibitions.description: Fifty years of photojournalism by Donna Ferrato (b. 1949), documenting the resilience of women, particularly survivors of domestic violence, from inside shelters and alongside law enforcement.
exhibitions.venue_address: 465 Huntington Avenue, Boston, MA 02115, United States

exhibitions.title: Hao Jingban: I Witness
exhibitions.description: Blending documentary sensibility with poetic construction, Hao Jingban makes moving-image installations that are emotionally precise, historically incisive, and formally experimental.
exhibitions.venue_address: Wiesner Building, 20 Ames Street, Bldg. E15-109, Atrium level, Cambridge, MA 02139, United States

exhibitions.title: Uri Aran: Look How Hard They Work
exhibitions.description: Uri Aran's work is at once deeply idiosyncratic and oddly familiar: to follow it is to tinker alongside the artist, to be let in on an invention, or perhaps a shorthand between friends.
exhibitions.venue_address: Wiesner Building, 20 Ames Street, Bldg. E15-109, Atrium level, Cambridge, MA 02139, United States

exhibitions.title: Robert Lazzarini: metes and bounds

exhibitions.title: Common Sense
exhibitions.description: An exhibition that puts America's past in dialogue with its present.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
exhibitions.long_description:
The rest is small: two of Thomas Paine's texts, a 1792 leatherbound Common Sense and a pamphlet of The American Crisis, no. 1, set against nine contemporary works. Öyvind Fahlström, Joyce Kozloff, Hank Willis Thomas and Kara Walker reframe American history, and Donald Moffett and Maynard Monrow made new text pieces with one message: power lies with us.

It is included in general admission, which is pay what you can at the desk (suggested $20, free for ages 19 and under). It closes November 8. Moffett's sound installation IMPEACH is the companion show.

look_for.title: The Commons
look_for.text: Look for the riderless cork horse, nearly 13 feet tall, shaped like an equestrian statue and built to collect visitors' pinned messages and keepsakes.

look_for.title: Paine on paper
look_for.text: A 1792 leatherbound edition of Common Sense and a pamphlet of The American Crisis, no. 1, the two texts the show is built around.

look_for.title: Kozloff's sing-along collage
look_for.text: Laboring slaves, Civil War soldiers, cotton fields and steamships, scattered with lyrics from slave songs and hymns taken from 1920s game boards her mother gave her.

exhibitions.title: Splendido, As Seen by Chris Rhodes
exhibitions.description: Twenty-seven photographs by Chris Rhodes of Belmond's Hotel Splendido above Portofino, from its interiors and landscape to its staff and guests.
exhibitions.venue_address: 380 Columbus Avenue at West 78th Street, New York, NY 10024
exhibitions.long_description:
Benedictine monks built the hilltop house above Portofino because they wanted to live as close to the sky as they could. It is now Belmond's Hotel Splendido, and in 2025 Belmond commissioned Chris Rhodes to photograph it. Twenty-seven of those pictures hang in Aperture's gallery on Columbus Avenue.

Rhodes moves between the picturesque and the everyday: the interiors, the gardens and the bay, and the staff and guests in between. Belmond's own feature on the series picks out fruit on a breakfast table and an empty tennis court alongside the views. You come for the Riviera and get its offbeat side as much as its scenery.

It's free and runs for twelve days only, 4 to 15 November, closed Monday and Tuesday. Belmond commissioned the work and is also the presenting sponsor of Aperture's 2026 Gala. The book of the photographs is on sale in the Aperture bookstore.

exhibitions.title: Pierre Huyghe: UUmwelt
exhibitions.description: Freestanding screens throughout the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden use machine learning and fMRI-derived data to generate hallucinatory images in real time, exploring nonhuman and machine cognition.
exhibitions.long_description:
Huyghe worked with neuroscientists at Kamitani Lab (Kyoto University) and ATR. A person imagined images in an fMRI scanner, and the network turned the scans into thousands of visual interpretations. They play on freestanding screens spread through the Sculpture Garden, with sound. A sensor tracks where visitors look, and simulated cancer-cell mutations feed in too, together deciding which images appear next. The Times Square billboards a few blocks north ignore you, but this is the one screen in Midtown that notices where you look.

It is outdoors, so dress for the weather. It runs until 29 November and is included with general admission, $30 for adults. Expect fragments rather than finished pictures.
exhibitions.editors_pick: Freestanding screens across MoMA's sculpture garden generate hallucinatory images in real time from machine learning and fMRI-derived data. The one MoMA show where you keep your coat on.

look_for.title: The gaze-reading screens
look_for.text: A sensor picks up where visitors are looking, and the imagery on the freestanding screens changes in real time as a result.

look_for.title: The tractor-or-oil-rig horizon
look_for.text: One visitor saw a blurry horizon with what looked like a tractor or an oil rig in the centre, the network's reading of a brain scan.

look_for.title: The cancer-cell sequencing
look_for.text: Simulated cancer-cell mutations help decide which images come next, so the sequence on the screens is never a fixed loop.

exhibitions.title: Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses
exhibitions.description: North American debut of Dutch couturier Iris van Herpen, with 140+ sculptural haute couture creations shown alongside contemporary art, design, and natural history specimens.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
exhibitions.long_description:
The chapters run from water to the cosmos by way of skeletons, fear and growth, with fossils, coral, beetles and a 1732 Ovid set beside the dresses. In the rotunda the museum rebuilt her Amsterdam atelier: you look down microscopes and handle fabric samples, which Interview's writer said "feels almost like a science museum." Near the end, a wall of photos shows who has worn her work, from Lady Gaga to Tilda Swinton.

The Philadelphia Inquirer's Bedatri Choudhury called it "an exercise in constant wonder and awe." Timed tickets are $30 for adults, include general admission and enter every 15 minutes; members go free. It closes December 6.

look_for.title: The Living Algae dress
look_for.text: Look for the 2025 look holding about 125 million bioluminescent algae in seawater, which light up blue as the wearer moves.

look_for.title: The Skeleton dress
look_for.text: A 2011 copper-plated, 3D-printed dress with its ribs splayed open, shown beside a 180-million-year-old marine reptile fossil; the Inquirer found it "at once exquisite and slightly eerie".

look_for.title: Bird
look_for.text: Hand-sewn layers of laser-cut silicone over ivory cotton, with three 3D-printed bird skulls hidden among the "feathers".

look_for.title: Seed of Narcissus
look_for.text: In the atelier rotunda, a crystal cocoon coated in beeswax honeycomb that thousands of bees built over several months.

look_for.title: The Cosmic Bloom gallery
look_for.text: Multicolored dresses hang from the ceiling, some mannequins upside down, to a soundscape by Salvador Breed.

exhibitions.title: Yoshitomo Nara
exhibitions.description: New paintings and drawings, recent sculptures, and early works spanning from the 1980s to today: the artist's first solo presentation with David Zwirner and his first major New York solo show in nearly a decade.
exhibitions.long_description:
You walk into the 533 West 19th Street gallery and thirteen heads look back. Each is a palm-sized clay head Nara modelled by hand, enlarged ten times in bronze and coated in matte white urethane. The press release says they recall the snow "monsters" that heavy snowfall built in the rural northern Japan of his childhood. They are the only snowmen in Manhattan this winter that won't end up as gray curb slush.

One block over at 537 West 20th Street are new 2026 paintings: front-facing portraits with direct gazes, in a palette the gallery says has turned more muted over the past year. Others start as colored-pencil sketches under thin acrylic washes, with tear-filled eyes. Large monochrome drawings in industrial paint stick sit beside works from the 1980s that Nara picked himself.

Entry is free, Tuesday to Saturday, 10am to 6pm, and the opening reception on 5 November, 6 to 8pm, is open to the public.

look_for.title: Thirteen white snow-monster heads
look_for.text: At 19th Street, look for bronze heads ten times the size of their hand-molded clay originals, their matte white surfaces catching light and shadow.

look_for.title: The new 2026 portraits
look_for.text: At 20th Street, front-facing figures stare straight at you through muted, layered color and soft, diffused brushwork.

look_for.title: Pencil-and-wash paintings
look_for.text: Colored-pencil drawings show through translucent acrylic washes, with figures in natural poses and tear-filled eyes.

look_for.title: Large paint-stick drawings
look_for.text: Big monochrome drawings in industrial oil-based paint stick, all bold line, unlike the hazy new paintings beside them.

exhibitions.title: Brice Marden: I Am Plane Image
exhibitions.description: A comprehensive survey of Brice Marden's paintings spanning six decades at the West 21st Street gallery, the first such show of his work in New York in twenty years, with major loans from the Art Institute of Chicago, the Whitney, and other collections.
exhibitions.long_description:
This is the first Marden survey in New York in twenty years, with loans from the Art Institute of Chicago and the Whitney. It starts with Nebraska (1966), painted after a cross-country trip, and ends with The Dance and Lingerie (2022 to 23), his last paintings. In between, geometry gives way to calligraphic networks drawn from Asian art. The Inferno review notes that "a gray can contain warmth, dirt, violet, green", which also describes the Hudson on a November afternoon, so walk west afterwards and check.

Vasili Kaliman wrote that "painting does not get much better than this". Admission is free. The Chelsea galleries are open Tuesday to Saturday, 10am to 6pm, and the show runs to 12 December.
exhibitions.editors_pick: From Nebraska (1966) to Marden's last paintings of 2022–23, with the six-panel Propitious Garden of Plane Image stretched across 24 feet. Loans from the Art Institute of Chicago and the Whitney, in a free Chelsea gallery.

look_for.title: Nebraska (1966)
look_for.text: The earliest painting in the show, based on Midwestern landscape from a cross-country trip; Marden kept it and hung it in his home.

look_for.title: Summer Table (1972-73)
look_for.text: Painted around his time on the Greek island of Hydra, in a brighter palette, with the beeswax-and-turpentine oil surface at its clearest.

look_for.title: Study for the Muses (Eagles Mere Version) (1991-99)
look_for.text: A large calligraphic painting made in his Pennsylvania studio, its colours echoing the woodland outside.

look_for.title: The Propitious Garden of Plane Image, Second Version (2000-06)
look_for.text: Six panels, 72 by 288 inches overall, moving through a colour progression taken from Chinese garden tradition.

look_for.title: The Dance and Lingerie (2022-23)
look_for.text: His last two large paintings, made in his Tivoli studio and shown together as in his final Gagosian show in 2023.

exhibitions.title: Jem Perucchini: Sospiro
exhibitions.description: New figurative paintings by Italian, Ethiopian-born Jem Perucchini (b. 1995), drawing on Renaissance painting, African wax prints and Ethiopian church frescoes. His first US exhibition.
exhibitions.long_description:
In Sospiro (2026), the painting the show is named after, a young figure with cropped dark hair looks sideways out of a speckled emerald-green field, dressed in the same green. The title is Italian for "sigh", which Perucchini calls "the passage between the inner self and the external world".

This is the Milan-based painter's first show in the US: new paintings of single figures and pairs, plus Icarus, Narcissus, Inanna and Gilgamesh, often under a glowing moon or sun. He sprays the canvases with an oil-based emulsion, which gives them their mottled skin. The two graphite drawings, each of a lone figure at a chessboard, are the first drawings he has shown in public. In Washington Square Park, a lone player at a chessboard is waiting for you to sit down.

There are no reviews yet, so go for the jewel-toned color and the slow, sidelong figures. Entry is free at 52 Walker Street in Tribeca, and the opening reception is Friday 6 November, 6 to 8pm.

look_for.title: Sospiro (2026)
look_for.text: The title painting: a young figure with cropped dark hair glances sideways out of a speckled emerald-green ground, wearing the same green.

look_for.title: The two chess drawings
look_for.text: His largest works on paper so far, in graphite, each showing one figure alone at a game of chess, and the first drawings he has shown in public.

look_for.title: The sprayed surfaces
look_for.text: Get close to the canvases to see the mottled, patina-like finish he builds by spraying them with an oil-based emulsion.

look_for.title: The mythic figures
look_for.text: Look for Icarus, Narcissus, Inanna and Gilgamesh among the new paintings, cast as the lithe, youthful figures he paints from imagination.

exhibitions.title: Li Hei Di: the year of mud
exhibitions.description: New paintings by London-based Li Hei Di, between figuration and abstraction, shaped by the myth of the goddess Nüwa shaping people from mud. Their first solo show with Pace in New York.
exhibitions.long_description:
Li Hei Di kept thinking about Nüwa, the Chinese goddess believed to have made people by dipping a rope in muddy water and swinging it, each flying drop landing as a person. Over a year of personal change, Li pictured their body as one of those drops. These new paintings came out of that year, and Li calls them "giant listeners" that held them through it.

The figures never settle, sliding between figuration and abstraction in a palette Pace calls almost shimmering, forms surfacing and receding. The hang is planned so that different works and pairings come into view as you move through the space. Anyone who has been sprayed by a cab on Tenth Avenue in December knows half of Nüwa's method.

It's Li's first solo show with Pace in New York, and no one has reviewed it yet. Entry is free at Pace's Chelsea building, 540 West 25th Street, from 6 November to 19 December, with an opening reception on 5 November from 6 to 8pm.

exhibitions.title: Bea Scaccia: Groomed
exhibitions.description: Bea Scaccia's debut exhibition with the gallery, at the Park & 75 space: seven new paintings of nocturnal, sumptuous scenes assembled from fabric, wigs, jewelry and other accoutrements of feminine style, curated by Francesco Bonami.
exhibitions.long_description:
The other six paintings work the same way. You look for figures and find wigs, costume jewelry, zippers, bows and faux fur bundled into puppet-like limbs in fishnet tights, trying to sit on chairs, climb ladders or lift dumbbells and never quite managing. Scaccia mixes gesso into acrylic to mute the colour, so every scene reads as night, lit by fringed lamps and precariously placed candles. It is the only place on Park Avenue where the accessories do the yoga.

The gallery points to Hans Bellmer's dolls, Mike Kelley and Sarah Lucas, so come if those are your references. Entry is free at Park & 75, 821 Park Avenue, Tuesday to Saturday 10am to 6pm, until 23 December.

look_for.title: Heels over Head, or Pillow Talk (2026)
look_for.text: The nine-foot diptych where Olympia's reclining nude becomes a heap of cloth and pillows on a bed, faceless but still holding up a book.

look_for.title: The figures that can't sit down
look_for.text: Look for surrogate bodies hovering over chairs without quite sitting, clutching dumbbells and twisted into yoga-like poses.

look_for.title: The ladder paintings
look_for.text: Cloth and accessories draped over ladders, climbing nowhere and hanging like marionettes.

exhibitions.title: David Byrne: Stairwell Drawings
exhibitions.description: Nine life-size drawings by Talking Heads' David Byrne line the stairwell landings between the flagship's first and seventh floors, reflecting his surreal, playful sensibility.
exhibitions.long_description:
The Talking Heads co-founder has been drawing since art school, and first showed with Pace in 2003. He told Artnet in January that a drawing expresses an idea "quickly and immediately", before reworking makes it more seductive and loses that. It's the rare Chelsea show where the elevator is the wrong way in.

The catch is that it's easy to miss: one visitor guide reckons half of Pace's visitors never see it. Walk up from the first floor. The stairwell closes while Pace installs new shows, as it did this summer until 10 September. Entry is free, and Pace lists the run to 31 December 2026 but says the drawings stay indefinitely.

exhibitions.title: Architects of Liberation: Modernism in Western Africa
exhibitions.description: The first major survey of modern architecture across seven West African nations from the late 1950s to the early 1980s, exploring how building shaped newly independent states. Most objects have never been shown publicly.
exhibitions.long_description:
About 450 drawings, models, photographs and films follow, most never shown publicly, from seven countries between the late 1950s and the early 1980s. The rooms move from dams and skyscrapers to trade fairs, then universities. You'll want to lean in on the reconstructed models: Architectural Record's critic got close enough that a docent asked for a step back. Midtown took the glass box as delivered; western Africa sent it back with edits.

Domus called it "a powerful, long-overdue chronicle". Architectural Record rated the last rooms, on trade fairs and universities, the strongest, but found the show "often avoids defining the intellectual concepts that made liberation meaningful". It's in the third-floor Menschel Galleries, included with $30 admission, until January 2, 2027.

look_for.title: The La Pyramide model
look_for.text: A model rebuilt by Cooper Union students shows Rinaldo Olivieri's Abidjan tower with its stepped pyramid facades and louvres angled against the sun.
