exhibitions.venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Parcours : André Malraux et Pablo Picasso, le musée imaginaire
exhibitions.description: A focus room on André Malraux's view of Picasso, born of his 1973 visit to the artist's last home and studio and his book La Tête d'obsidienne.

exhibitions.title: Prix Marcel Duchamp 2026
exhibitions.description: The four 2026 nominees for France's leading contemporary art prize (Andrianomearisoa, Brognon Rollin, Henno, Ntjam) show work within the MAM's collections. Winner announced 22 October 2026.
exhibitions.venue_address: 11 Avenue du Président Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Kurt Schwitters. Le chaos-monde, 1918-1948
exhibitions.description: First Kurt Schwitters retrospective in France in over thirty years: 300+ works and documents, from Merz collages to the Ursonate, set beside his affinities with Picasso's assemblage.

exhibitions.title: Wild Heart
exhibitions.description: Sonia Gomes's textile-based sculptures draw on Afro-Brazilian heritage, transforming fabric and craft into vehicles of memory, care and resistance.
exhibitions.venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Ali Cherri: Today Is Ok
exhibitions.description: French-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri presents the film "La Sentinelle" and a new installation on military service and its psychological effects, following a soldier suspended between destiny and self-abandon.
exhibitions.venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Rose Lowder: The Source of the Loire and Other Films
exhibitions.description: Filmmaker Rose Lowder's fifty-year research into visual perception through nature observation, centred on her film "La Source de la Loire" (2019-2021) alongside twenty one-minute films shot on organic farms in southern France.
exhibitions.venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Fragments of Paris: Jacques Villeglé and Urban Art
exhibitions.description: A retrospective marking the centenary of Jacques Villeglé, tracing his practice of collecting torn Parisian street posters and reworking them into art that documents the city's changing urban and cultural landscape.

exhibitions.title: Photoromance
exhibitions.description: The first major French solo show of Ivorian photographer Paul Kodjo, co-produced with Les Rencontres d'Arles: his 1970s photo-novels and documentary images of Abidjan.
exhibitions.venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Valerie John: I Telman Nwe Ki I Ble (So Black It Turns Blue)
exhibitions.description: Valerie John explores indigo blue as material, memory and artistic gesture, with assemblages of paper, textiles and objects tracing cultural ties between Martinique and West Africa.
exhibitions.venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Lassana Sarre: Globale Inversion Inversion
exhibitions.description: Painter Lassana Sarre creates wall paintings and looped sound installations celebrating the overlooked routines and shared meals of the Palais de Tokyo's security staff.
exhibitions.venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: You and Your Gang
exhibitions.description: A group exhibition of individual and collective artistic practices rooted in non-urban territories across France, including Limousin, the Cevennes and Corsica.
exhibitions.venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Contemporary Counterpoint: Vija Celmins
exhibitions.description: The museum's 17th Contemporary Counterpoint: Vija Celmins's precise studies of ocean, desert, sky and snow surfaces, made 1971-2000 in drawing, painting, printmaking and wood engraving, shown in the pronaos and contemporary gallery in dialogue with Monet's Water Lilies.
exhibitions.venue_address: Jardin des Tuileries, Côté Seine, 75001 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Louise Bourgeois: Extreme tension
exhibitions.description: The BnF and Centre Pompidou combine their Louise Bourgeois holdings for the first time - some 200 drawings, prints and artist's books - in the artist's first Paris public-institution show since 2008. At the BnF Richelieu, Galerie Mansart.

exhibitions.title: Jenny Holzer. J'ai vu
exhibitions.description: A museum-wide activation by American artist Jenny Holzer: LED installations, facade projections and carved stone benches drawing text from Orsay's 1848-1914 collection.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Echoes of the Tides
exhibitions.venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
exhibitions.description: An installation by Yo-E Ryou in the music box of the Collections Plateau, unfolding through sound, breath and duration to explore resonance between bodies, water and memory.

exhibitions.title: The Harvest Season - Ibrahim Mahama
exhibitions.description: Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama's first major French show, with nine associate artists, reactivating African independence-era utopias through monumental installations made from salvaged materials.

exhibitions.title: Moteur Imaginaire
exhibitions.description: Large's opening show, curated by Cecilia Alemani: works from Renault's art collection beside 17 new commissions, over 100 works by 55 artists on humans, factories and machines.
exhibitions.venue_address: 3 parvis Amont, Île Seguin, 92100 Boulogne-Billancourt, France

exhibitions.title: Susan Meiselas: Nicaragua, History, Memory
exhibitions.description: Meiselas's 1978-79 Sandinista revolution photographs and how they took on a life of their own on objects and murals: 100+ works, documents and film clips, curated by Clément Chéroux.

exhibitions.title: Martine Franck: Images, Press and Feminist Struggles
exhibitions.description: Mostly unpublished photographs by Martine Franck of 1970s feminist movements, mainly in Paris: protests and the feminist press. Curated by Angèle Ferrere.

exhibitions.title: Gustave Fayet, Collector - Designer. Icons of Modern Art
exhibitions.description: Rediscovery of Gustave Fayet (1865-1925), pioneering collector of van Gogh, Gauguin and Picasso and a prolific designer, drawing on loans from 64 institutions and 71 private collections.
exhibitions.venue_address: 8 Avenue du Mahatma Gandhi, 75116 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Primeval Waters: Lessons from Mesopotamia
exhibitions.description: An exploration of ancient Mesopotamia's relationship with water, tracing early canals and aqueducts and the environmental consequences of humanity's first great hydraulic engineering.

exhibitions.title: Paolo Cirio: NUDIFY AI
exhibitions.description: An online commission in which Paolo Cirio investigates non-consensual AI-generated sexual imagery, turning 15,000 collected deepfakes into an anonymised visual database.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1 place de la Concorde, Jardin des Tuileries, 75001 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Louvre Photo
exhibitions.description: Over 300 photographs tracing the Louvre's own history, from the invention of photography to today, showing the museum as subject, model and source of inspiration.

exhibitions.title: Lady Liberté. De la sueur, de l'audace, du génie
exhibitions.description: An immersive look at how the Statue of Liberty was built in 1880s Paris, tracing the copper, iron and ingenuity, including Gustave Eiffel's internal frame, behind the Franco-American monument.

exhibitions.title: Transparency
exhibitions.description: Inaugural show of the new Palais des enfants: a playful, sensory journey where artworks and science experiments play with light to spark the curiosity and wonder of very young visitors.
exhibitions.venue_address: Avenue du Général Eisenhower, 75008 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Guillermo Kuitca, Chapelle
exhibitions.description: A site-specific installation by Argentine artist Guillermo Kuitca in the chapel of the Hôtel Salé, where his "cubistoid" intersecting lines are painted directly onto the walls to form a new pictorial space.

exhibitions.title: New Paris, from 1977 to the Present Times
exhibitions.description: A free display in the 1977-to-today room on how Paris has changed since its first elected mayor, with recent acquisitions by Christo and Jeanne-Claude, JR and others.

exhibitions.title: Silent Violence: Through the Eyes of Romeo Mivekannin
exhibitions.venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
exhibitions.description: Artist Romeo Mivekannin uses mirror effects and metal sculptures to examine the history of colonial exhibitions and human zoos, reinterpreting historical ethnographic photographs from the museum's collection.

exhibitions.title: Gustave Le Gray, Painter and Photographer
exhibitions.description: A "Bicentennial of Photography" retrospective on Gustave Le Gray (1820-1884), the painter-turned-photographer and technical innovator, featuring newly surfaced acquisitions shown for the first time.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Travail, ce que disent les objets
exhibitions.description: A capsule show in which some thirty Cnam and CNRS researchers pick everyday work objects, from office chair to badge and post-it, illustrated by Romain Joly, to show how work is changing.

exhibitions.title: Révéler. Collection de photographie du Centre Pompidou
exhibitions.description: About a hundred works by some thirty artists from the Centre Pompidou's photography collection, shown at the Grand Palais during Paris Photo 2026 for the bicentenary of photography.

exhibitions.title: De Gaulle avant de Gaulle
exhibitions.description: Charles de Gaulle's early military and literary career, 1909 to 1940, before his famous June 1940 appeal, told through letters, manuscripts, photographs and personal objects.
exhibitions.venue_address: Hôtel national des Invalides, 129 rue de Grenelle, 75007 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Le Musée imaginaire d'Oli
exhibitions.description: The rapper Oli (Bigflo & Oli) stages his inner museum: about a hundred works and new installations, laid out as a coming-of-age journey with sound as the thread.
exhibitions.venue_address: Avenue du Général Eisenhower, 75008 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: David Gilbert — Apparitions
exhibitions.description: The first French solo exhibition of American artist David Gilbert, gathering fifteen years of work at the intersection of photography, sculpture and installation: studio-built assemblages of paper, fabric and found objects photographed as fragile, twilight-lit tableaux.

exhibitions.title: Girls. Adolescence, Fashion and Rebellion
exhibitions.description: Artists, designers, photographers and filmmakers challenge traditional representations of teenage girls through multidisciplinary works spanning fashion, photography, film and contemporary art.
exhibitions.venue_address: Avenue du Général Eisenhower, 75008 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Édouard Vuillard
exhibitions.description: A Room 33 display of recent Vuillard gifts, including two overdoor panels completing the Public Gardens series and pieces from the Schopfer dinner service.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Mika Ninagawa with EiM: Alive with Shadows
exhibitions.description: An unprecedented European exhibition of Japanese visual artist Mika Ninagawa's work alongside her creative collective EiM, exploring beauty, transience and the interplay of light and shadow through photography, video and installations.
exhibitions.venue_address: Avenue du Général Eisenhower, 75008 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Le sentiment du monde. Carte blanche au Centre Pompidou
exhibitions.venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
exhibitions.description: The Centre Pompidou hangs works by several generations of artists inside the museum's permanent route, setting formal echoes and critical reinterpretations of tradition against the collections.

exhibitions.title: Aïnous. Une voix du Japon
exhibitions.venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
exhibitions.description: The first exhibition by a French national museum on the Ainu, Indigenous people of northern Japan. Contemporary Indigenous art links past and present, with loans from Japan's national Ainu museum.

exhibitions.title: William Klein: New York Revisited
exhibitions.description: Klein's 1954-55 New York photographs, drawn from his studio's documents: icons of 20th-century photography and many images the tight layout of the 1956 book hid, with the first full reading of this body of work.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1 place de la Concorde, Jardin des Tuileries, 75001 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Jonathas de Andrade: Tropical Hangover and Other Stories
exhibitions.description: The Brazilian artist's relationship to the image, through key projects of the past decade in photography, video and installation.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1 place de la Concorde, Jardin des Tuileries, 75001 Paris, France

exhibitions.title: Frankenstein Pop-Up
exhibitions.description: The museum's popular Frankenstein pop-up returns for spooky season, on view on select Saturdays from September through November.
exhibitions.venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

exhibitions.title: An Endless Meeting: Featuring Caroline Woolard
exhibitions.description: Caroline Woolard's installation brings together works from "A Stone Holds Water" (2020) and "Art of Gravity" (2026).
exhibitions.venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

exhibitions.title: An Endless Meeting: Collective Process, Artistic Labor, and the Politics of Working Together
exhibitions.description: New Red Order, Kameelah Janan Rasheed and Caroline Woolard each approach collaboration, shared knowledge and collective action through distinct forms.
exhibitions.venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

exhibitions.title: An Endless Meeting
exhibitions.description: Vox's autumn project on collective process, artistic labour and the politics of working together, spanning exhibitions, a curatorial residency, public programmes and a print publication.
exhibitions.venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

exhibitions.title: An Endless Meeting: Featuring New Red Order
exhibitions.description: New Red Order's "Give it Back: Crimes Against Realty (Office Edition)" is a real estate office and recruitment station encouraging the rematriation of land to Indigenous people.
exhibitions.venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

exhibitions.title: An Endless Meeting: 變 SLOW BURN
exhibitions.description: Eight artists and collectives work through memory, grief, queer kinship and transformation in installation, performance, video, sound and painting, drawing on fènghuáng mythology.
exhibitions.venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

exhibitions.title: An Endless Meeting: Still Taking Minutes
exhibitions.description: Curated by Logan Cryer, an interview-based show about how Philadelphia artists build, sustain and leave collectives, with new work by Aaron Terry, Ollie Goss, Gregory Donnell Parker and catia colagioia.
exhibitions.venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

exhibitions.title: Revolutionary Botany
exhibitions.description: Marking America's 250th birthday, this show traces the origins of American pharmacy and botanical medicine in the city that called itself the birthplace of American medicine.
exhibitions.venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

exhibitions.title: The Philly Killer
exhibitions.description: Summer 1976: as Philadelphia threw America's Bicentennial party, a deadly unidentified pneumonia struck. The true story of Legionnaires' disease.
exhibitions.venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

exhibitions.title: Kati Gegenheimer: We've Only Just Begun
exhibitions.venue: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
exhibitions.description: A Morris Gallery monographic show in which Gegenheimer's vivid paintings and mixed-media works treat love, familial and romantic, as an aesthetic and political structure rather than a sentiment.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102, United States

exhibitions.title: Marketing Medicine: The Art of Selling a Cure
exhibitions.description: Two centuries of medical trade ephemera show how jingles, patient testimonials and celebrity endorsements taught medicine to sell itself.
exhibitions.venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

exhibitions.title: Creating a City of Medicine
exhibitions.description: 250 years of Philadelphia's impact on how Americans have learned, taught, practised and experienced medicine, told through the College's own archive.
exhibitions.venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

exhibitions.title: Creative Processing: Art in Therapy
exhibitions.description: How making art became a formal clinical practice, from 1940s pioneers to today's 8,000 credentialled art therapists, and the work patients made along the way.
exhibitions.venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

exhibitions.title: The Photo Review: Best in Show 2026
exhibitions.description: Prizewinning pictures from The Photo Review's 41st International Photography Competition, juried by Sarah Kennel of the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts.
exhibitions.venue_address: 9201 Germantown Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19118, United States

exhibitions.title: Pennsylvania's Founding: How a City and a Colony Shaped America's Civic DNA
exhibitions.description: Free show with Drexel University on how Penn's 1681 "holy experiment" and the planned city of Philadelphia shaped American civic habits, with Atwater Kent artefacts and student-built map and timeline interactives.
exhibitions.venue_address: 525 Arch Street, Philadelphia, PA 19106, United States

exhibitions.title: PAW Patrol: Adventure Play
exhibitions.description: Children join the PAW Patrol pups on rescue missions around Adventure Bay: launching alerts from the Lookout Tower, driving rescue vehicles, serving at Porter's Cafe and climbing Jake's Mountain.
exhibitions.venue_address: Memorial Hall, 4231 Avenue of the Republic, Philadelphia, PA 19131, United States

exhibitions.title: The Declaration's Journey
exhibitions.description: Over 120 artifacts, including six historic printings of the Declaration of Independence, trace how its promise of liberty travelled the world from 1776 to today.
exhibitions.venue_address: 101 South Third Street, Philadelphia, PA 19106, United States

exhibitions.title: You Stretched Diagonally Across It: Contemporary Tapestry
exhibitions.description: Works by around two dozen international artists treat tapestry as a conceptual space, weighing authenticity, slow labour against technological speed, and how to depict vastness.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1214 Arch Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

exhibitions.title: Noguchi to Asawa: Designing Postwar America
exhibitions.description: Sculpture and design by six Japanese American artists (Isamu Noguchi, George Nakashima, Leo Amino, S. Neil Fujita, Kay Sekimachi and Ruth Asawa) whose work reshaped modern American design after WWII incarceration.
exhibitions.venue_address: 2025 Benjamin Franklin Parkway, Philadelphia, PA 19130, United States

exhibitions.title: Arc of Promise
exhibitions.description: Marking America's 250th anniversary, this show traces how Philadelphia artists have imagined "America" as an idea, from the founding era to the present.
exhibitions.venue_address: 9201 Germantown Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19118, United States

exhibitions.title: Listen with Your Eyes: A Moe Brooker Retrospective
exhibitions.description: Woodmere's first retrospective of Moe Brooker (1940–2022), from 1960s realism to rainbow patchwork abstractions swept with calligraphic marks, plus sculpture, weavings and personal material.
exhibitions.venue_address: 9201 Germantown Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19118, United States

exhibitions.title: Sky Hopinka: Red Metal Dust
exhibitions.description: A site-specific installation of 11 new video, photography and text works by Sky Hopinka (Ho-Chunk Nation/Pechanga Band), interrogating American histories and Indigenous homelands in the Annenberg Court.
exhibitions.venue_address: 2025 Benjamin Franklin Parkway, Philadelphia, PA 19130, United States

exhibitions.title: Rodin's Hands
exhibitions.description: Fifteen bronzes and plasters, many rare or unique to Philadelphia, trace Rodin's obsession with the expressive hand, from The Cathedral and The Hand of God to Two Hands.
exhibitions.venue_address: 2151 Benjamin Franklin Parkway, Philadelphia, PA 19130, United States

exhibitions.title: Marcel Duchamp
exhibitions.description: The first North American Duchamp retrospective in over fifty years: more than 300 works across six decades, from painting and sculpture to film, photography and the readymades.
exhibitions.venue_address: 2600 Benjamin Franklin Parkway, Philadelphia, PA 19130, United States

exhibitions.title: Native Plants on the Parkway: A Botany of Nations Garden
exhibitions.venue: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University
exhibitions.description: An outdoor living demonstration garden on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway planted with species native to Northeastern North America, extending the Botany of Nations story outside.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1900 Benjamin Franklin Parkway, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

exhibitions.title: Botany of Nations
exhibitions.venue: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University
exhibitions.description: Retells the Lewis and Clark expedition through Indigenous ecological knowledge, pairing the Academy's historic Lewis and Clark Herbarium specimens with contemporary Native voices.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1900 Benjamin Franklin Parkway, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

exhibitions.title: From the School Collection
exhibitions.venue: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
exhibitions.description: Plaster casts and cast drawings spanning more than 140 years, showing how classical models have underpinned training at America's oldest art school since 1805.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102, United States

exhibitions.title: Proof Testing: The PrintLab Artist Residency at Brandywine Workshop and Archives
exhibitions.venue: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
exhibitions.description: Eight interdisciplinary artists pair finished prints with the working materials behind them, showing the PrintLab residency as an incubator for traditional printmaking and emerging technologies alike.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102, United States

exhibitions.title: The Condition of Being Near
exhibitions.description: Group exhibition on solidarity across Black, African and Chinese diasporic networks, with video, installation, prints and archival works by nine artists.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118 S. 36th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States

exhibitions.title: Waste Scenes: Maia Chao and Fred Schmidt-Arenales
exhibitions.description: A two-channel video made during a residency at a Philadelphia recycling centre, staging performative vignettes choreographed by discarded materials.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118 S. 36th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States

exhibitions.title: Wilmer Wilson IV: SKIRL!
exhibitions.description: ICA's inaugural R+D residency: Wilmer Wilson IV takes the eastern gray squirrel as a lens on American ecologies and colonial history, in installation, sculpture and performance.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118 S. 36th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States

exhibitions.title: To Be Continued...
exhibitions.venue: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
exhibitions.description: Unfinished paintings, sketches and studies from PAFA's permanent collection, treating incompletion not as failure but as evidence of experiment and material process.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102, United States

exhibitions.title: Fred Wilson: THE MASTER PLAN or In Between the Big Bang and Modern Art Is the Restroom
exhibitions.venue: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
exhibitions.description: Twenty-two photogravures reproducing the floor outlines of major museums' visitor maps, questioning the museum as a neutral repository and how its architecture shapes what we see.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102, United States

exhibitions.title: In This Academy: Selected Works from the Permanent Collection
exhibitions.venue: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
exhibitions.description: Prominent American artists who studied or taught at PAFA, from traditional realism to contemporary practice, tracing the visual languages the school has produced since 1805.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102, United States

exhibitions.title: A Nation of Artists
exhibitions.description: The museum's America-250 centrepiece: over 1,000 works tracing three centuries of American art making, drawn from its own collection and the Middleton Family Collection.
exhibitions.venue_address: 2600 Benjamin Franklin Parkway, Philadelphia, PA 19130, United States

exhibitions.title: A Nation of Artists
exhibitions.venue: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
exhibitions.description: Reopening the Historic Landmark Building for PAFA's 220th anniversary: over 1,000 works from the late 18th century to today, including 100+ pieces from the Middleton Family Collection.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102, United States

exhibitions.title: Open Video Call 2026
exhibitions.description: ICA's relaunched biannual platform for moving-image work by Delaware Valley artists, screened on the mezzanine across a fall and a spring season.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118 S. 36th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States

exhibitions.title: Entryways: Saif Azzuz
exhibitions.description: Yurok artist Saif Azzuz fills ICA's Sansom Street windows with abstract graphics drawn from research into Philadelphia's natural history.
exhibitions.venue_address: 118 S. 36th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104, United States

exhibitions.title: Seeking Profit and Power: Philadelphia, China Trade, and the Making of America
exhibitions.description: Around 150 rarely seen objects trace how the young United States, cut off from British trade after the Revolution, turned east to China and built itself into a global economic power.
exhibitions.venue_address: 211 S. Columbus Blvd., Philadelphia, PA 19106, United States

exhibitions.title: Rochelle Feinstein: The Today Show
exhibitions.description: More than 30 mixed-media works by Rochelle Feinstein on abstraction, culture and public life, including 11 large-scale pieces commissioned by the Barnes for the Annenberg Court.
exhibitions.venue_address: 2025 Benjamin Franklin Parkway, Philadelphia, PA 19130, United States

exhibitions.title: Radka Bodzewicz: FAUST
exhibitions.description: Paintings interpreting Goethe's Faust through Jungian archetypes of desire for knowledge, love, power and fame.

exhibitions.title: Květa Kovářová – For the Shape of the Figure
exhibitions.description: Retrospective tracing sculptor Květa Kovářová's path from 1950s figurative works to 1960s abstract and architectural commissions, highlighting an overlooked woman artist of post-war Czechoslovak sculpture.
exhibitions.venue_address: U Sovových mlýnů 503/2, 118 00 Prague 1 – Malá Strana, Czech Republic

exhibitions.title: Czech Press Photo 2025
exhibitions.description: Nearly 800 award-winning and nominated photojournalism images from the 31st Czech Press Photo competition, shown across nine categories in the New Building's Brutalist travertine hall.

exhibitions.title: New Caledonia: An Archipelago at a Crossroads
exhibitions.venue: Náprstek Museum of Asian, African and American Cultures
exhibitions.description: A courtyard photography exhibition by Dr Karolina Kania documenting New Caledonia's history, identity and multicultural society.

exhibitions.title: Anna Polanská & Pavla Vachunová: Before the Stone Blooms
exhibitions.description: Glass and ceramic works by Anna Polanská and Pavla Vachunová in a silent dialogue exploring nature, memory and craftsmanship.

exhibitions.title: Familiar and Unfamiliar Vietnam
exhibitions.venue: Náprstek Museum of Asian, African and American Cultures
exhibitions.description: Vietnam's history, traditions and contemporary culture, developed with the Vietnamese community in the Czech Republic.

exhibitions.title: Crested/mâcistan: Tanya Lukin Linklater and Duane Linklater
exhibitions.description: First major European joint show by these First Nations artists, with sculpture, installation and painting on Indigenous land, trade and erased histories, woven with Czech glass beads.

exhibitions.title: A Life Dedicated to Pragas. A Tribute to Emil Příhoda
exhibitions.description: Eight restored Praga vehicles from Emil Příhoda's private collection, shown alongside a borrowed Praga Alfa and motoring awards honouring the collector.

exhibitions.title: Terra Incognita
exhibitions.description: At the House of Photography: video essays and installations on how media and measurement technologies shape our perception of the Earth as a resource for extraction.
exhibitions.venue_address: Mariánské náměstí 98/1, 110 00 Prague 1 – Staré Město, Czech Republic

exhibitions.title: 230 Years of the NGP
exhibitions.venue: National Gallery Prague – Trade Fair Palace
exhibitions.description: A mini-exhibition marking 230 years since the founding of the Society of Patriotic Friends of the Arts, with 70 works from all five NGP collections tracing the gallery's history and acquisitions.

exhibitions.title: Milan Kunc – Pop Renaissance
exhibitions.description: Works from the 1980s alongside contemporary paintings by Milan Kunc, blending pop-cultural aesthetics, irony and surrealist imagination to explore consumerism, ideology and identity. Curated by Filip Kazda.
exhibitions.venue_address: U Sovových mlýnů 503/2, 118 00 Prague 1 – Malá Strana, Czech Republic

exhibitions.title: Design for Václav Havel
exhibitions.description: Marking Havel's 90th birthday, this Riding School show presents the first post-Communist president through the objects that surrounded him: Bořek Šípek's furniture and glass, Theodor Pištěk's Castle Guard uniforms, and Havel's own study.

exhibitions.title: Mikuláš Medek, Jan Koblasa – In Defiance
exhibitions.description: Photographs by Jiří Hampl with works by Medek and Koblasa from 1959-63, marking Medek's centenary and commemorating a 1963 Teplice show of existential abstract art suppressed under communist rule.
exhibitions.venue_address: U Sovových mlýnů 503/2, 118 00 Prague 1 – Malá Strana, Czech Republic

exhibitions.title: ANDROS
exhibitions.description: Group show of around 50 Central European artists examining depictions of the male body and modern masculinity, curated by Vratislav Maňák.

exhibitions.title: Chronos. The Theme of Time in 16th- to 18th-Century Prints
exhibitions.description: Prints from the NGP's Collection of Prints and Drawings tracing the allegorical figure of Chronos, "Father Time," from triumphs of time to William Hogarth's satires and Josef Bergler's New Year cards.

exhibitions.title: What Made The Railways, What the Railways Made
exhibitions.description: The story of modern rail transport as an engine of global change, told through authentic exhibits, interactive elements and artworks.

exhibitions.title: Jaroslav Čermák: Myths of European Reality

exhibitions.title: Annette Messager: Tragikomedie

exhibitions.title: The Dark Blue World of Jaroslav Ježek
exhibitions.description: Marking the 120th anniversary of composer Jaroslav Ježek's birth, twelve sections trace his life from student years through the Liberated Theatre to American exile.

exhibitions.title: Anna Jagiellon (1503–1547): Queen on the Threshold of a New Era
exhibitions.venue: National Gallery Prague – Wallenstein Riding School
exhibitions.description: Marking 500 years since the Habsburgs' accession to the Bohemian throne, this show traces the life of Queen Anna Jagiellon through Renaissance portraits and works by Cranach, Dürer and Titian.

exhibitions.title: David Tibet: Hallucinate, Children
exhibitions.description: Retrospective of drawings and paintings by David Tibet, founder of Current 93, featuring recurring visionary motifs of children, angels and apocalyptic landscapes.

exhibitions.title: Argus & Medusa: On Hope in Dark Times
exhibitions.description: Contemporary artists respond to Géricault's "The Raft of the Medusa," exploring hope and solidarity amid war, displacement and ecological crisis.

exhibitions.title: Point of View 4: Resilience
exhibitions.description: Fourth instalment of DOX's Point of View series, exploring resilience as a quiet, relational form of resistance through contemporary art.

exhibitions.title: Vojta Náprstek Reloaded
exhibitions.venue: Náprstek Museum of Asian, African and American Cultures
exhibitions.description: Over 420 artifacts mark the 200th anniversary of founder Vojta Náprstek's birth, exploring his life, American travels and role as a champion of technological progress and women's rights.

exhibitions.title: Milada Schmidtová: Putting My Dreams and Desires into Pictures, into Words…
exhibitions.description: At the Stone Bell House: the first comprehensive retrospective of this overlooked Central European post-war painter, who withdrew from public life after brief recognition in the 1940s.

exhibitions.title: Gaia De Megni: Maria's Dream
exhibitions.venue: MACRO - Museum of Contemporary Art of Rome

exhibitions.title: Robin Rimbaud (Scanner): 52 Spaces
exhibitions.venue: MACRO - Museum of Contemporary Art of Rome
exhibitions.description: British artist and composer Robin Rimbaud deconstructs and reassembles dialogue, sound effects and music from Antonioni's 1962 film L'eclisse, layered with ambient recordings of Rome's streets into a contemplative acoustic fabric.

exhibitions.title: WWF Italia. Rivoluzione Naturale
exhibitions.venue: MAXXI - National Museum of 21st Century Arts
exhibitions.description: Six decades of WWF Italia's influence on how the country thinks about nature, from Fulco Pratesi's early vision and the first reserves to major species campaigns. In the Corner MAXXI.

exhibitions.title: States of Uncertain Domesticities
exhibitions.description: An international group show of around 30 works (video, paintings, sculpture and installations) exploring contemporary domesticity through a feminist, political and social lens, touching on housing, migration and environmental crisis.

The itinerary, introduced by a monumental replica of the Trojan Horse, connects the heritage of ancient Ilion with the myth of Aeneas and the founding of Rome.
exhibitions.venue_address: Piazza del Colosseo, 1, 00184 Roma RM, Italy

exhibitions.title: MACRO. Museum of the Everyday
exhibitions.venue: MACRO - Museum of Contemporary Art of Rome
exhibitions.description: Nine projects by IED interior design students reimagine MACRO as a museum open to everyday life, with spaces for learning, work and collective rituals.

exhibitions.title: Vitalita dell'architettura italiana 1946-2026
exhibitions.venue: MAXXI - National Museum of 21st Century Arts
exhibitions.description: An 80-year survey of Italian architectural ideas, projects and visions, tracing eight decades of the Republic from the post-war years to contemporary practice and future scenarios.

exhibitions.title: Miriam Cahn: Ciò che mi guarda
exhibitions.venue: MACRO - Museum of Contemporary Art of Rome
exhibitions.description: The Swiss artist's first major museum retrospective in Italy: 100+ works from the late 1970s on, anchored by the room installations Herumliegen and Familienraum, exploring the body, war and desire.

exhibitions.title: Moda in luce 1955-1975. Roma fra glamour e innovazione industriale

exhibitions.title: Le Litanie della Vergine di Mario Deluigi. Dialogue between the Sacred and Abstraction
exhibitions.description: Deluigi's abstract "Litanies of the Virgin Mary (Homage to Mondrian)" with its 1972 silkscreen portfolio, a sketch notebook and two Rubelli textile panels. At the Papal Palace of Castel Gandolfo.

exhibitions.title: AEGYPTUS. Dal Nilo al Mediterraneo. Oasi e deserto in epoca romana
exhibitions.description: Immersive video-art and AI installation on the Roman presence in Egypt's western desert oases, with archaeological finds, in the Octagonal Hall of the Baths of Diocletian (Museo dell'Arte Salvata).

exhibitions.title: Marina Bindella. Cosmografie
exhibitions.description: Around forty works by Marina Bindella (paintings, woodcuts, watercolours and large polyptych installations made from 2020 onward) exploring mark-making as a generative principle of form, light, space and cosmic structure.
exhibitions.venue_address: Viale Fiorello La Guardia 6, 00197 Rome, Italy

exhibitions.title: Fuochi sul Tevere: Roma attraverso gli occhi di Kanutas Ruseckas
exhibitions.description: The Castellan's apartment hosts a selection of paintings by 19th-century Lithuanian Romantic painter Kanutas Ruseckas, part of the Italy-Lithuania 2026 cultural year, exploring Rome's pull on European artists.

exhibitions.title: Luigi & Iango. Corpi speciali

exhibitions.title: Luchino Visconti e la messa in scena della storia

exhibitions.title: La donazione Ennio Calabria
exhibitions.venue: La Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

exhibitions.title: Contiamo l'Italia, contiamo per il futuro

exhibitions.title: Titian. Dialogues between the Sacred and the Profane

exhibitions.title: Diego Rivera and the Construction of Modern Art in 20th-Century Mexico

exhibitions.title: Artista alla GNAMC. Marinella Senatore: Protagonista 2026

exhibitions.title: Martin Malvar: For Your Amusement

exhibitions.description: Two ceramic masters, Swedish and Japanese, united by a love of clay and glaze and beautiful everyday objects for all; also explores cultural exchange as soft power.

exhibitions.title: City Faces
exhibitions.description: Historical portraits, biographical records and facial recognition bring Stockholm's 19th-century faces, from maids to wholesalers, back to life.

exhibitions.title: Monir Shahroudy Farmanfarmaian – Tehran/New York
exhibitions.description: Around 100 works from 1970–2015: kaleidoscopic mirror mosaics, geometric sculptures, collages, rugs and her "Heartache Boxes".

exhibitions.title: Jan Håfström – The Lost World
exhibitions.description: An exhibition of Swedish artist Jan Håfström, curated by Matilda Olof-Ors.

exhibitions.title: Life in Color & Form: Robert and Barbro Nilsson
exhibitions.description: Retrospective of sculptor Robert Nilsson, a Milles pupil, and textile pioneer Barbro Nilsson of Märta Måås-Fjetterström: sketches, weaving samples, models and letters.

exhibitions.title: True Crime
exhibitions.description: Sweden's prohibition era in 1920s-30s Stockholm, told through smugglers, bootleggers and moonshiners.

exhibitions.title: Current Archaeology: Finds from Sylta
exhibitions.description: Entrance-hall showcase of fresh excavation finds, currently objects from a Viking Age burial ground at Sylta near Köping, Västmanland.

exhibitions.title: INNER CHILD: Playing with Design
exhibitions.description: Lidewij Edelkoort and Philip Fimmano curate 100 designers and artists, among them Maarten Baas, Front and Yinka Ilori, in eight chapters on play, imagination and making by hand.

exhibitions.title: Democracy does not exist - We make it!
exhibitions.venue: Medelhavsmuseet (Museum of Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities)
exhibitions.description: Interactive show built with V-Dem research and personal stories, exploring fair elections, freedom, equality, openness and participation.

exhibitions.title: Byggfenomen: The First and Last Thing We See
exhibitions.description: Architect Daniel Johansson moves humble acoustic ceiling tiles onto the wall in a full-scale installation, turning an overlooked everyday material into ornament.

exhibitions.title: Diana Markosian: Father
exhibitions.description: Diana Markosian's personal photographic story of separation, absence and reunion with her father.

exhibitions.title: James Cameron – Challenging the Deep
exhibitions.description: Europe's first showing of James Cameron's deep-sea exploits: film props from Titanic and Avatar, his underwater cameras and the tech behind his record dives.

exhibitions.title: Absolut Absolut
exhibitions.description: A spectacular advertising story: how a Swedish state enterprise made Absolut Vodka a global icon, told through some 90 bottles, 130 ads and a robot-run cocktail bar.

exhibitions.title: Colour! For children and their curious grown-ups
exhibitions.description: An immersive, hands-on exhibition for ages 6-12: don a lab coat and colour goggles and explore what colour is, where it comes from and how it feels.

exhibitions.title: Sara-Vide Ericson: DRIFT
exhibitions.description: Around sixty new works Sara-Vide Ericson painted aboard the icebreaker Oden in the Arctic Ocean, from monumental canvases to installations with expedition material.

exhibitions.title: Gingerbread House 2026
exhibitions.description: ArkDes' beloved Christmas show: a city of gingerbread towers and houses by amateurs and professionals, with public voting and prizes.

exhibitions.title: Menu Prints – Where Art Meets Science
exhibitions.description: Signed original prints by Swedish artists made for the Nobel medicine laureates' dinner menus, shown with a table set with the Nobel dinner service.

exhibitions.title: Kvinnor bakom kameran, 1848–1968
exhibitions.description: Women behind the camera: rewriting Swedish photography history with long-overlooked work by female professional photographers.

exhibitions.title: Nobel Creations 2026
exhibitions.description: First-year fashion students at Beckmans College of Design create free interpretations of this year's Nobel Prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, peace and economics.

exhibitions.title: Maria Bonnier Dahlins Stiftelses stipendiater 2026
exhibitions.description: Major show of the 2026 Maria Bonnier Dahlin Foundation grant winners Henrik Jonsson, Rakel Bergman Fröberg and Tekla Bergman Fröberg, marking the prize's 40th year.

exhibitions.title: Women as Technology
exhibitions.description: Over a hundred design objects and hi-tech artefacts show how women have been made to embody ideas of computing power, domestic work, fertility and satisfaction.

exhibitions.title: Black Myth
exhibitions.description: Drawing on the video game Black Myth: Wukong and the novel Journey to the West, this show curated by David Williams explores myth, transformation and the dark side of modern China through works by Sun Xun, Xu Zhen, Zhu Jinshi and others.

exhibitions.title: Remy Faint: A Site of Unfolding
exhibitions.description: Remy Faint's most comprehensive body of work yet, spanning painting, sculpture and installation, exploring personal histories and cultural memory through silk, clay, wood and metal.
exhibitions.venue_address: Cnr Oxford St & Greens Rd, Paddington NSW 2021, Australia

exhibitions.title: Heather B. Swann: The Forests of Symbols
exhibitions.description: Newly commissioned and rarely seen sculpture, painting and drawing by Heather B. Swann, the first in a final series exploring symbolism and allegory.
exhibitions.venue_address: Cnr Oxford St & Greens Rd, Paddington NSW 2021, Australia

exhibitions.title: Jordan Gower: Does the moon know the well?
exhibitions.description: The inaugural institutional exhibition of South Australian ceramic artist Jordan Gower, exploring functional craft and contemporary art through layered glazes and repetition.
exhibitions.venue_address: Cnr Oxford St & Greens Rd, Paddington NSW 2021, Australia

exhibitions.title: Michael Muir: The Shape of Colour
exhibitions.description: Survey of Northern Beaches painter Michael Muir's past decade, tracing his vibrant, memory-laced landscapes through colour, form and composition.

exhibitions.title: Girly in Manly
exhibitions.description: Kate Bohunnis, Anne Ferran, Maddison Gibbs and Ebony Russell explore femininity, inheritance and place, starting from the colonial naming of Manly.

exhibitions.title: Andy Ewing: Ancestor Spirits / Kirthana Selvaraj: In the Half Light
exhibitions.description: A posthumous survey of queer Vietnamese-Australian artist Andy Ewing (1964-2021) paired with new commissions by inaugural Andy Ewing Fellow Kirthana Selvaraj, on inheritance, queerness and the body.

exhibitions.title: Angus Nivison: Unfamiliar Territory
exhibitions.description: A five-decade survey of abstract landscape painter Angus Nivison, curated by Rachel Parsons and touring from New England Regional Art Museum.
exhibitions.venue_address: Watson Road, Observatory Hill, The Rocks, Sydney NSW 2000

exhibitions.title: David Hockney: Bigger & Closer (not smaller & further away)
exhibitions.description: Immersive 360-degree projection experience by Lightroom London spanning six decades of David Hockney's work, narrated by the artist with a score by Nico Muhly.

exhibitions.title: Hayley Millar Baker: No Spectacular Soul
exhibitions.description: Multi-screen video installation critiquing systems that decide whose lives are deemed worthy of protection, centring Indigenous voices asserting rights to resistance and survival.
exhibitions.venue_address: 43-51 Cowper Wharf Road, Woolloomooloo NSW 2011, Australia

exhibitions.title: Nolan: Origins
exhibitions.venue: Art Gallery of New South Wales
exhibitions.description: A major survey of over 150 works from Sidney Nolan's formative Australian years, including the 1946-47 Ned Kelly series.
exhibitions.venue_address: Art Gallery Road, The Domain, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

exhibitions.title: Dana Claxton: Headdress
exhibitions.description: Hunkpapa Lakota artist Dana Claxton's first international First Nations Banner Series commission, pairing regalia-adorned portraiture with redacted FBI surveillance files on Indigenous activism.
exhibitions.venue_address: 43-51 Cowper Wharf Road, Woolloomooloo NSW 2011, Australia

exhibitions.title: Just Because: CAO Yu
exhibitions.description: Ideas Platform show of multidisciplinary work by Beijing artist CAO Yu, using her own image, fallen hair and urine to probe gendered expectations and beauty ideals.
exhibitions.venue_address: 43-51 Cowper Wharf Road, Woolloomooloo NSW 2011, Australia

exhibitions.title: Robyn Kahukiwa: My Ancestors Are Always With Me
exhibitions.description: A survey of Māori artist Robyn Kahukiwa's paintings addressing Indigenous identity, sovereignty and whakapapa.
exhibitions.venue_address: 140 George Street, The Rocks, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

exhibitions.title: 2026 Australian Geographic Nature Photographer of the Year
exhibitions.description: 100 award-winning nature photographs from Australia, New Zealand, Antarctica and New Guinea, produced by the South Australian Museum.

exhibitions.title: Connections: MCA x Tate
exhibitions.description: Contemporary art from the shared collections of the MCA Australia and Tate Modern, London, including works by Yhonnie Scarce.
exhibitions.venue_address: 140 George Street, The Rocks, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

exhibitions.title: Chronos: Australian Ceramics from 1933
exhibitions.description: Traces a century of Australian ceramic practice from the earliest piece in MAG&M's collection, presenting clay as a medium that stores and transmits cultural memory.

exhibitions.title: 200th Anniversary Exhibitions: Amaze Gallery
exhibitions.venue: State Library of New South Wales
exhibitions.description: Marking the Library's bicentenary, over 200 items on display including the Endeavour journals and a 1297 copy of the Magna Carta.
exhibitions.venue_address: Macquarie Street & 1 Shakespeare Place, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

exhibitions.title: Migrating Modernism: The Architecture of Harry Seidler
exhibitions.description: Traces architect Harry Seidler's path from Nazi-occupied Vienna and studies with Gropius and Breuer to a major Australian career, with drawings, models and photographs.

exhibitions.title: Ai Weiwei: Neil Balnaves Tallawoladah Lawn Commission 2026
exhibitions.description: A new large-scale outdoor sculpture commission by Chinese artist Ai Weiwei for the MCA's Tallawoladah Lawn.
exhibitions.venue_address: 140 George Street, The Rocks, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

exhibitions.title: Definitive Dupain
exhibitions.venue: State Library of New South Wales
exhibitions.description: A landmark retrospective of Max Dupain's complete body of work, drawn from the Library's archive of over 250,000 negatives and prints.
exhibitions.venue_address: Macquarie Street & 1 Shakespeare Place, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

exhibitions.title: Terraforming: Works from the Gene & Brian Sherman Collection
exhibitions.description: Six pioneering Chinese contemporary artists, including Ai Weiwei and Xu Bing, who reshaped China's creative landscape after 1976, from the Sherman family's collection.

exhibitions.title: Fibre Optics: First Nations women in fibre
exhibitions.description: Celebrates the artistry and technical mastery of First Nations women's fibre works from Arnhem Land, the Torres Strait and Boggabilla, presented as masterworks rather than craft.

exhibitions.title: Tracey Moffatt: Sorted – a look at her Archive
exhibitions.description: The first archive of its kind donated to an Australian museum, tracing photographer and filmmaker Tracey Moffatt's career since 1985 through photo series, films and ephemera.

exhibitions.title: Philippe Parreno: 5 Moons
exhibitions.description: Sydney International Art Series 2026-27: a major survey of French artist Philippe Parreno's immersive film, light and sound installations.
exhibitions.venue_address: 140 George Street, The Rocks, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

exhibitions.title: Chromatic Luminosity
exhibitions.description: Nine contemporary abstract painters explore how light and glow can be crafted on canvas, reclaiming a quality screens haven't replicated.

exhibitions.title: The Grad Show 2026
exhibitions.description: The National Art School's major end-of-year exhibition of Bachelor of Fine Art graduate work across ceramics, drawing, painting, photomedia, printmaking and sculpture.

exhibitions.title: Takashi Murakami: When the Mountain Is High, the Moon Rises Higher
exhibitions.venue: Art Gallery of New South Wales
exhibitions.description: Australia's first major Murakami retrospective, spanning three decades of his Superflat paintings, sculpture and installation.
exhibitions.venue_address: Art Gallery Road, The Domain, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia

exhibitions.title: Colorful Asia: Journey through Asia at Tokyo National Museum
exhibitions.description: A tour of the Asian Gallery (Toyokan) exploring artworks through the lens of color, pigment science, and dyeing techniques across Asia.

exhibitions.title: NHK Taiga Drama Special Exhibition: Brothers in Arms
exhibitions.description: Renewal-commemorative special exhibition on brothers Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Hidenaga's role unifying Japan, with artifacts tied to Nobunaga, Ieyasu and Sen no Rikyu.

exhibitions.title: Masterpieces from the Itsuo Art Museum Collection: Buson, Go Shun, and the Art of Tea
exhibitions.description: First major Tokyo showing in ~30 years of the Itsuo Art Museum's collection, from classical calligraphy fragments and tea utensils to paintings by Yosa Buson and Matsumura Go Shun.
exhibitions.venue_address: Tokyo Midtown Galleria 3F, 9-7-4 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-8643, Japan

exhibitions.title: Suikoden: The Water Margin, Outlaws of the Marsh
exhibitions.description: Traces the classic Chinese novel Suikoden from Song-dynasty origins through its Edo-period popularity in Japan, with Ming and Qing works, Kuniyoshi's ukiyo-e, manga, and drama costumes.

exhibitions.title: The Beauty of Coolness: Edo-Tokyo Museum Glass Craft Collection
exhibitions.description: Themed display of edo-kiriko and satsuma-kiriko cut glass vessels made for samurai and wealthy townspeople, blending Japanese and Western decorative styles.

exhibitions.title: Possibilities of A Piece of Cloth: TYPE-XVII JAXA Project by A-POC ABLE ISSEY MIYAKE
exhibitions.description: Gallery 3 show exploring body and clothing through a JAXA satellite image of Antarctica, which inspired A-POC ABLE ISSEY MIYAKE's jacquard-woven textiles for extreme environments including space.

exhibitions.title: Best of the Sumida Hokusai Museum: The Sumida River Landscape Scroll and Other Masterpieces
exhibitions.description: 10th-anniversary special exhibition featuring a seven-metre Sumida River scroll back in Japan after a century, plus rare and newly acquired Hokusai works.

exhibitions.title: Kimura Ihei Photography Award 50th Anniversary Commemorative Exhibition
exhibitions.description: Commemorative exhibition marking the 50th edition of Japan's prestigious Kimura Ihei Photography Award; full details to be announced by the museum closer to opening.

exhibitions.title: Bugaku Costumes: The Enduring Beauty of Textiles
exhibitions.description: Special exhibition of lavish Bugaku court-dance costumes from temples and shrines including Amano-sha and Rinnoji, some shown for the first time in decades.

exhibitions.title: Memory of Topography
exhibitions.description: A seasonal light installation evoking shifting terrain and landscape, on display at teamLab Borderless from September through November.
exhibitions.venue_address: Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza B B1, 5-9 Toranomon, Minato-ku, Tokyo

exhibitions.title: Katsushika Ōi "Night Scene in the Yoshiwara" — The Lineage of Nightscapes
exhibitions.description: Two-term exhibition tracing ukiyo-e depictions of nighttime scenes, centred on Katsushika Ōi's famous "Night Scene in the Yoshiwara."

exhibitions.title: Tada Minami—Still, Shimmering Light
exhibitions.description: First Tokyo solo show in 35 years for sculptor Tada Minami (1924-2014), spanning sculpture, chandeliers and architectural "light sculptures" across her 70-year career.

exhibitions.title: Daitokuji: A Zen Temple Beyond Compare
exhibitions.description: Treasures from Daitokuji, the Kyoto Zen temple founded in 1326, and its sub-temples, shown for its 700th anniversary and including the Kizaemon Ido tea bowl (National Treasure).

exhibitions.title: Synchronic Constellation: Cross-Boundary Perspectives in Art
exhibitions.description: Roughly 200 modern Taiwanese artworks, archival material and contemporaneous Japanese pieces, exploring shared modernity across art, film, literature and music.

exhibitions.title: Masterpieces of the Renaissance from the Musée du Louvre
exhibitions.description: Over 50 Louvre masterpieces trace 15th-16th century Renaissance art, including the Japan debut of Leonardo da Vinci's "Portrait of a Woman" (La Belle Ferronnière).

exhibitions.title: Albert Marquet: A Retrospective
exhibitions.description: Some 90 works by the French Fauvist, tracing his career and celebrated waterside scenes and Pont-Neuf series, on loan from major French museums.

exhibitions.title: Marimekko: Art of Printmaking — Beauty, Dream, Love
exhibitions.description: Over 60 dresses, printed textiles and production materials from the Finnish design house Marimekko, with a video on its Helsinki print factory and work by designer Akira Minagawa.

exhibitions.title: Seeds and Roots: How to Cultivate a City
exhibitions.description: Group show of contemporary Japanese artists exploring the ecosystems that adapt to city life, from roadside weeds to organisms coexisting with concrete.

exhibitions.title: project N 104: Tanaka Ai
exhibitions.description: Tanaka Ai (b. 1992) shows large mineral-pigment paintings on paper, including the 2026 Acting in the Phenofact pair, in the gallery's emerging-artist series.

exhibitions.title: Scenes of Autumn: From the Terada Collection 088
exhibitions.description: Autumn-themed works from the gallery's Terada Collection, including paintings by Nambata Tatsuoki, Matsumoto Yuko and Uchida Aguri.

exhibitions.title: Hiroshige: New Perspectives on Edo Japan
exhibitions.description: Special exhibition marking the gift of the Uchiyama Susumu collection, showing complete sets of Hiroshige's Tokaido, Kiso Road, and Edo landscape print series in rotation.

exhibitions.title: Learning from "Hōjōki": Tiny Architecture Reweaves Life
exhibitions.description: Contemporary architects and designers reinterpret Kamo no Chōmei's 13th-century "Hōjōki" and its 9m² hermitage, rethinking what it means to dwell. Directed by architect Yoshiharu Tsukamoto.

exhibitions.title: "Shōwa 100th": How Conservation and Restoration Evolved at the NMWA during the Shōwa Period — Van Gogh's Roses and Renoir's Woman with a Hat

exhibitions.title: Amis de Paris: Japanese Artists in Paris
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo
exhibitions.description: MOMAT Collection Focus show on Japanese artists who lived in Paris from the pre-war era through the postwar period, including Fujita Tsuguharu and Okamoto Taro.

exhibitions.title: Picturing the Theater: From Delacroix and Daumier to Toulouse-Lautrec and Klinger
exhibitions.description: About 50 prints and drawings, plus three paintings, by 19 artists show how nineteenth-century Paris theatre, from Delacroix's Shakespeare to Toulouse-Lautrec's posters, entered art.

exhibitions.title: Takehisa Yumeji—An Artist Who Defined His Era
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo
exhibitions.description: Special exhibition of 500 works and materials by Takehisa Yumeji (1884-1934), covering his "Yumeji style" images of women, paintings, prints and graphic design.

exhibitions.title: Assembling Anew: Emerging Japanese Artists vol.23
exhibitions.description: Five contemporary artists using AI, CG and stop-motion reassemble existing memories, materials and technologies into new imagery, questioning how we perceive information today.

exhibitions.title: Duet: Asian Contemporary
exhibitions.description: Six photographers and video artists from China and Japan in dialogue, exploring resonances born from the intersection of different cultures, times and personal experiences.

exhibitions.title: Fontanesi: Italian Light, Landscapes of the Heart
exhibitions.description: First major retrospective in Japan in 50 years of Italian landscape painter Antonio Fontanesi (1818-1882), who taught early Japanese Western-style painters in Tokyo.

exhibitions.title: The Light Spreads Out, and Glittering Things Start Appearing All Around Me
exhibitions.description: Kusama's work seen through the theme of light, from 1950s drawings to recent mirror rooms and metallic sculptures where light becomes the work itself.

exhibitions.title: The Strangers' Gaze: Japanese Artists in Europe
exhibitions.description: Over 100 paintings from the Ishibashi Foundation Collection show how Japanese artists studying in Europe since the Meiji era, including Kuroda Seiki and Fujita Tsuguharu, engaged with Western art traditions.

exhibitions.title: Jam Session: The Ishibashi Foundation Collection x Fujii Hikaru "WHOSE LIGHT?"

exhibitions.title: Shojo Manga Infinity: Moto Hagio, Ryoko Yamagishi, and Waki Yamato
exhibitions.description: A retrospective on three pioneering shojo-manga artists, tracing their careers from the late 1960s to today through original drawings and archival material.

exhibitions.title: Turner: Painting the Sublime, in Dialogue with Contemporary Art
exhibitions.description: A special exhibition placing J.M.W. Turner's work in dialogue with contemporary art, exploring the sublime in landscape and light.

exhibitions.title: Sex in Nature (生きものたちの性)
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of Nature and Science
exhibitions.description: The museum's first special exhibition on sex as a theme, covering the diversity of sex in animals and plants through form, behaviour, sex determination and parenting.

exhibitions.title: Challenging Infectious Diseases: Past, Present and Future (Noguchi Hideyo 150th Anniversary)
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of Nature and Science
exhibitions.description: A commemorative exhibition marking 150 years since the birth of bacteriologist Noguchi Hideyo, tracing his life's work and humanity's ongoing fight against infectious disease.

exhibitions.title: MAM Screen 024: Jakrawal Nilthamrong
exhibitions.description: Three films by Thai artist Jakrawal Nilthamrong, centred on Rhizome (2022), where a man drifts on a raft above a flooded world. Screened 18:00-22:00, about 39 minutes in total.
exhibitions.venue_address: Roppongi Hills Mori Tower 53F, 6-10-1 Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo 106-6150, Japan

exhibitions.title: MAM Project 035: Brie Ruais
exhibitions.description: New ceramic sculptures by Santa Fe-based Brie Ruais, made after a residency at Shigaraki and research into Japanese clay and ceramic history, shaped through full-body movement.
exhibitions.venue_address: Roppongi Hills Mori Tower 53F, 6-10-1 Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo 106-6150, Japan

exhibitions.title: Mori Art Award 2026 Grand Prize Exhibition: Katayama Mari
exhibitions.description: Showcase for Katayama Mari, first Grand Prize winner of the Mori Art Award, whose analogue photography, embroidery and needlework extend the boundaries of her own body.
exhibitions.venue_address: Roppongi Hills Mori Tower 53F, 6-10-1 Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo 106-6150, Japan

exhibitions.title: Mariko Mori: All That Shines
exhibitions.description: Japan's first major Mariko Mori retrospective since 2002, spanning three decades from her 1990s Cyborg series to recent installations shaped by Buddhist philosophy and science.
exhibitions.venue_address: Roppongi Hills Mori Tower 53F, 6-10-1 Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo 106-6150, Japan

exhibitions.title: The Studio of Yuriko Yamawaki: Treasure from an Artist's Clutter
exhibitions.description: Recreation of illustrator Yuriko Yamawaki's studio, exploring her picture-book collaborations with Rieko Nakagawa and her influence on Hayao Miyazaki.

exhibitions.title: What a Wonderful World: Masterworks from the Musée d'Orsay
exhibitions.description: Around 110 works from the Musée d'Orsay spanning painting, sculpture, decorative arts and photography, including Monet, Van Gogh and Renoir.

exhibitions.title: Ways of Reading—How the World Speaks to Us, How We Speak to the World
exhibitions.description: Free 100th-anniversary thematic show pairing sculpture, photography, text and painting by five artists exploring dialogue with the world.

exhibitions.title: The History of the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum
exhibitions.description: Free 100th-anniversary archives exhibition retracing the museum's century through documents, photographs and the people behind it.

exhibitions.title: Nikolai Astrup: Creating a Garden
exhibitions.description: Retrospective of about 130 works by the Norwegian painter Nikolai Astrup, including oil paintings and woodblock prints depicting seasonal landscapes near Jolster Lake, Norway.

exhibitions.title: New Works Competition and Exhibition 2026
exhibitions.description: The museum's annual juried competition and sale of new handicrafts by contemporary makers, spanning ceramics, textiles, woodwork, lacquer, glass, metal, bamboo, straw and paper.

exhibitions.title: Okada Atsushi: Phantom Horse (Yururi Island 1950-2026)
exhibitions.description: Photographer Okada Atsushi's exhibition on Yururi Island, spanning 1950 to 2026, in the museum's basement-floor galleries.

exhibitions.title: Lacquerware with Carvings
exhibitions.description: Museum collection exhibition on East Asian lacquer techniques built on carving: chōshitsu, Kamakurabori, sōkin, tenshitsu and kinma.

exhibitions.title: The Art of the Lotus Sutra: To Create Is to Pray
exhibitions.description: Lavishly decorated sutras, Buddhist statues and paintings inspired by the Lotus Sutra, tracing how devotion to the text shaped Japanese art from antiquity to today.
exhibitions.venue_address: Tokyo Midtown Galleria 3F, 9-7-4 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-8643, Japan

exhibitions.title: Lesser-Known Masters of Ukiyo-e
exhibitions.description: A survey spotlighting overlooked ukiyo-e artists working in the shadow of the medium's most famous names.

exhibitions.title: Hokusai Crossover: Gathering in Sumida Across the Ages
exhibitions.description: 10th-anniversary show of Hokusai's Sumida views and the works born of his exchanges with Ota Nanpo and other writers, plus Hokusai prints that inspired later authors such as Masaoka Shiki.

exhibitions.title: Yanagi Soetsu: The Collecting Story (90th Anniversary)
exhibitions.description: 90th-anniversary show on how museum founder Yanagi Soetsu collected the folk crafts that make up the Mingeikan.

exhibitions.title: Neverending Journeys: FINAL FANTASY 40th Anniversary Exhibition
exhibitions.description: A 40th-anniversary showcase in the Hyokeikan tracing the FINAL FANTASY series through art and music, staged alongside the museum's historical Japanese collection.

exhibitions.title: The 130th Anniversary of the Birth of Togo Seiji: A Retrospective
exhibitions.description: About 100 paintings by Togo Seiji, from early avant-garde works to late large oils, with around 100 pieces of his commercial design for the museum's 50th year.

exhibitions.title: Time for Love and Prayers: Lithuanian Hand Crafts
exhibitions.description: Traditional Lithuanian handicrafts displayed across the museum's main building and annex.

exhibitions.title: Kaj Franck Retrospective: Timeless Finland Design
exhibitions.description: About 250 works by Finnish designer Kaj Franck (1911-1989), in glass, porcelain and fabric, with sketches and film, drawn mainly from the Design Museum Helsinki collection.

exhibitions.title: Material Ecstasy: From the Terada Collection 089
exhibitions.description: Postwar Japanese artists and how they treated material, from prewar abstraction pioneers to Gutai and Mono-ha, drawn from the gallery's Terada Collection.

exhibitions.title: project N 105: Sugawara Kaho
exhibitions.description: Sugawara Kaho's paintings, drawings, blueprints and field journals recording wild birds and their plumage, in the 4th-floor corridor.

exhibitions.title: The Tale of Genji: Radiant Culture of the Japanese Imperial Court
exhibitions.description: Paintings and crafts depicting scenes from The Tale of Genji, with manuscripts, commentaries and its spread into performing arts and popular culture, organised with Kyoto National Museum.

exhibitions.title: The Art History of the Pleasure Quarters
exhibitions.description: Exhibition tracing how ukiyo-e artists depicted Edo's licensed pleasure quarters over the centuries.

exhibitions.title: Buddhist Sculptures at the Nezu Museum
exhibitions.description: Museum collection exhibition presenting an overview of the Nezu's Buddhist sculpture holdings, among the finest of any private art museum in Japan.

exhibitions.title: Time
exhibitions.description: An exhibition treating the gallery as "one large clock," scattering time-related devices and design objects to examine how time structures daily life. Directed by graphic designer Tomohiro Okazaki.

exhibitions.title: Yebisu International Festival for Art & Alternative Visions 2027
exhibitions.description: The 19th edition of the museum's annual international festival of images and art, across its third, second and basement floors, with new work by four finalists.

exhibitions.title: Collaboration with Sunpride Foundation
exhibitions.description: International exhibition co-organized with the Sunpride Foundation, drawing on works from the foundation's collection, loans from artists and newly commissioned pieces.

exhibitions.title: Hans Haacke
exhibitions.description: The first large-scale retrospective in Asia of Hans Haacke, covering works and projects on environmental issues and critiques of political and corporate power.

exhibitions.title: Montmartre: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, Suzanne Valadon, and Lesser-Known Parisian Painters
exhibitions.description: The Montmartre art scene of the late 19th and early 20th century, through works by Toulouse-Lautrec, Suzanne Valadon and lesser-known painters of their circle. Title is tentative.

exhibitions.title: MOT Annual 2026
exhibitions.description: The 21st MOT Annual, bringing together emerging artists from contemporary art, performing arts and experimental music, with an emphasis on performances engaging personal and social memory.

exhibitions.title: 140th Birth Anniversary: Textile Artist Yamaga Seika
exhibitions.description: First retrospective in 40 years of dyeing and weaving artist Yamaga Seika (1885-1981), inventor of "hand-woven brocade," spanning traditional motifs to unconventional subjects like rockets.

exhibitions.title: ARTIZON NOW: Expanding, Connecting, the Collection
exhibitions.description: A showing of the museum's recent acquisitions, from first-ever public displays of ukiyo-e prints and Noh costumes to Western and Japanese modern art, contemporary and Aboriginal art, and design.

exhibitions.title: Static and Noise
