exhibitions.description: The first show devoted to the women artists in the Albertina's collection, from medieval convent woodcuts to early feminist work of the 1970s.

exhibitions.title: Seeds: Reclaiming Roots, Sowing Futures
exhibitions.description: Main show of the Klima Biennale Wien: 13 international artists, including Cecilia Vicuña and Kapwani Kiwanga, use sculpture, installation, photography and video to explore seeds, loss and regeneration.

exhibitions.title: Elisabeth von Samsonow
exhibitions.description: First large-scale survey of the Austrian artist-philosopher: sculptures, paintings, drawings, films and a site-specific installation on the earth as bearer of history, life and memory.

exhibitions.title: Shara Hughes: Sink In
exhibitions.description: Fever-dream landscapes by US painter Shara Hughes: giant flowers, enchanted forests and blazing sunsets in fauvist, expressionist colour.

exhibitions.title: Feminist Futures Forever
exhibitions.description: Artists from the feminist avant-garde to today tackle social, gender and ecological issues, building on the landmark 1985 show Kunst mit Eigen-Sinn.

exhibitions.title: ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRUCTION KITS 1890–1990: Plenty to Play With!
exhibitions.description: About 150 building kits from a century of toy-making, from wood and metal to Galalith and Lego, with eight hands-on stations where visitors can play and build.

exhibitions.title: The Special Case of Steffy Goldner: The New York Philharmonic's First Woman
exhibitions.description: In the Dorotheergasse Project Space: Nives Widauer's installation on Vienna-raised harpist Steffy Goldner, projected onto a historic harp case.

exhibitions.title: Farbenspiel. Mode aus vier Jahrhunderten
exhibitions.description: A cultural history of colour told through around 350 garments from the Wien Museum's fashion collection, exploring colour as a symbol of status, emotion and identity.

exhibitions.title: Franz West: The Revolution of Sculpture
exhibitions.description: Retrospective marking Franz West's 80th birthday, centred on his Adaptives: sculptures meant to be worn and handled that blurred art and everyday life.

exhibitions.title: CARLONE CONTEMPORARY: Asta Gröting. Things
exhibitions.description: Asta Gröting's video installation sends deformed everyday objects floating in slow motion through a deep blue summer sky, shown in the Upper Belvedere's Carlone Hall.

exhibitions.title: Crime Scene Ephesus: Cleopatra and Rome
exhibitions.description: A KHM show on the unsolved murder behind an octagonal tomb in Ephesus, set among Cleopatra, Caesar, Mark Antony and Augustus. In the Neue Hofburg.

exhibitions.title: No Way Home: Viennese Jews in Exile
exhibitions.description: At Museum Judenplatz: how Vienna stripped its Jews of their rights after 1938 and drove them out, and the lives of those who fled.

exhibitions.title: Temporary. Structures of Necessity
exhibitions.description: KOSMOS architects look at the temporary structures that keep cities running, from construction sites to maintenance work, and what they reveal about efficiency and adaptability.

exhibitions.title: Documents of Injustice. The Case of Freud
exhibitions.description: The Freud family's last months in Nazi Vienna: the dispossession of Sigmund and Alexander Freud and the murder of their four sisters, told through newly acquired documents.

exhibitions.title: Raining Blood. Photography and Arms Trafficking
exhibitions.description: Photos of c.1900 arms dealers, collection objects and contemporary art trace the global gun trade and challenge colonial myths of 'primitive' weapons.

exhibitions.title: TO SHOE OR NOT TO SHOE. Warhol and others
exhibitions.description: Cabinet show on the women's shoe as fetish, projection surface and site of feminist critique: Andy Warhol's shoe prints alongside Birgit Jürgenssen, Gudrun Kampl and Sylvie Fleury.

exhibitions.title: OPEN SPACE: A Room for Many Voices
exhibitions.description: A participatory room where communities from across Vienna reflect on the world and the museum, with three invited artists. Free admission.

exhibitions.title: Caution, high voltage! Electrical accidents – a class of their own
exhibitions.venue: Natural History Museum Vienna (Naturhistorisches Museum Wien)
exhibitions.description: At the NHM's Narrenturm site (Spitalgasse 2, 1090), a show on electropathology: Vienna's pioneering research, electricity's effects on the body, first aid and prevention.

exhibitions.title: Franz West and Vienna
exhibitions.description: How his home city shaped Franz West, focused on his formative years from the late 1960s to the early 1980s. Opens alongside a parallel West show at the Albertina Modern.

exhibitions.title: Hidden Stories: Treasures from the Collections
exhibitions.description: Objects from the Weltmuseum's stores that have rarely, if ever, been on public display, with the stories of where they came from and what they meant.

exhibitions.title: Good Collecting – Bad Collecting. 150 Years of the Natural History Museum Vienna
exhibitions.venue: Natural History Museum Vienna (Naturhistorisches Museum Wien)
exhibitions.description: The anniversary show traces how a 30,000-object imperial collection grew into 30 million, and looks critically at the darker sides of collecting and exploration.

exhibitions.title: GENchangers: Unraveled Secrets from Early Medieval Burial Grounds
exhibitions.venue: Natural History Museum Vienna (Naturhistorisches Museum Wien)
exhibitions.description: Genetics and archaeology reveal family ties in two early medieval burial grounds near Vienna, retelling the Migration Period through ordinary people's lives. Hall 21.

exhibitions.title: tierisch menschlich
exhibitions.description: The close yet ambivalent bond between animals and humans, from the Middle Ages to today, with works by Goya, Ensor, Maria Lassnig, VALIE EXPORT and Graciela Iturbide.

exhibitions.title: Tec/xtil
exhibitions.description: Fibre, function, fashion: a special exhibition taking clothing textiles apart into fibres, yarns and fabrics, from 19th-century objects to today's overproduction and textile waste.

exhibitions.title: Senon Williams: Further/Farther
exhibitions.description: A monumental mural triptych made for the Showroom Berggasse 19, picturing inner worlds, with Jane McAdam Freud's wire-mesh egg in an armchair at its centre.

exhibitions.title: Arnulf Rainer
exhibitions.description: Tribute to Arnulf Rainer (1929-2025), the uncompromising Austrian innovator whose radical 1950s overpaintings pushed painting to its limits.

exhibitions.title: More. Renata Poljak
exhibitions.description: Solo show in the Project Room Garage on the sea as a link between islands, migration and ecological crisis. It opens the Aqua cycle on water in motion.

exhibitions.title: Civa 2026: postacceleration
exhibitions.description: The sixth edition of the Civa biennial: five international artists push back against speed and optimisation, with talks, film screenings and live performances.

exhibitions.title: New. Objective: Photography of the 1920s and 30s
exhibitions.description: Over 100 photographs of the sober, clear New Objectivity, from Renger-Patzsch, Sander and Blossfeldt to Austrians like Trude Fleischmann.

exhibitions.title: Tiffany Sia: Overt Listening
exhibitions.description: Tiffany Sia's first Austrian solo show: a new film on the Cold War legacy of Taiwan's Kinmen Islands, bunkers, beaches and radio. At MuseumsQuartier.
exhibitions.venue_address: Museumsplatz 1, 1070 Vienna, Austria (second venue: Treitlstraße 2, 1040 Vienna)

exhibitions.title: Push and Pull: A Furniture Comedy
exhibitions.venue: mumok – Museum moderner Kunst Stiftung Ludwig Wien
exhibitions.description: Allan Kaprow's 1963 participatory piece, in which visitors rearrange furniture, anchors a show on collective action and the museum as a temporary studio.

exhibitions.title: A Different Beauty: Japanese Ceramic Masterworks
exhibitions.description: Rough, asymmetrical tea-ceremony ceramics from Bizen, Hagi and Shigaraki, made by generations of master-potter families, from the Heinz Slunecko collection.

exhibitions.title: The Imperial Family. Private Life and Duty at the Court of Francis II/I
exhibitions.venue: State Hall of the Austrian National Library (Prunksaal)
exhibitions.description: Letters, gifts and portraits reveal the household of Emperor Francis II/I and Empress Maria Teresa behind the idyll, under dynastic pressure and the threat of war.

exhibitions.title: Good architecture needs good clients
exhibitions.description: BHP26 ON TOUR: the winners and nominees of Austria's 2026 Client Award, which honours projects built through close collaboration between clients and architects.

exhibitions.title: Jewish Orientalists
exhibitions.description: At Dorotheergasse: how 19th-century Viennese Jewish scholars and adventurers shaped Oriental and Islamic studies while searching for their own origins.

exhibitions.title: Magali Reus: Tenant
exhibitions.description: Magali Reus's first Austrian solo show: vessel-like sculptures mixing casting, forging, wicker and embroidery with machine processes. At MuseumsQuartier.
exhibitions.venue_address: Museumsplatz 1, 1070 Vienna, Austria (second venue: Treitlstraße 2, 1040 Vienna)

exhibitions.title: Bernini, Painter and Sculptor
exhibitions.description: A KHM show at Palais Lobkowitz built around a Portrait of an Old Man newly attributed to Gian Lorenzo Bernini, with about ten international loans.

exhibitions.title: 100 BESTE PLAKATE 25: Deutschland Österreich Schweiz
exhibitions.description: The 21st edition of the best posters from Germany, Austria and Switzerland, from experimental author graphics to corporate design. In the MAK Plakat Forum.

exhibitions.title: Kunsthalle Wien Preis 2026: Lotti Brockmann & Valentino Skarwan
exhibitions.description: Joint show of the 2026 prize winners, recent graduates of Vienna's Academy of Fine Arts and University of Applied Arts. At Karlsplatz.
exhibitions.venue_address: Museumsplatz 1, 1070 Vienna, Austria (second venue: Treitlstraße 2, 1040 Vienna)

exhibitions.title: Iza Tarasewicz
exhibitions.description: Polish artist Iza Tarasewicz builds large modular installations from salvaged materials, drawing on philosophy, quantum physics and chaos theory.

exhibitions.title: Beaux Mendes
exhibitions.description: LA-based painter Beaux Mendes questions landscape painting's ties to power and colonialism in paintings and sculptures made during a Vienna residency.

exhibitions.title: Yoshinori Niwa
exhibitions.description: Vienna-based Japanese artist Yoshinori Niwa stages participatory, performance-based works that probe power, participation and society.

exhibitions.title: Verena Paravel: Cosmofonia
exhibitions.venue: mumok – Museum moderner Kunst Stiftung Ludwig Wien
exhibitions.description: An immersive film and sound project that tunes into the planet's inaudible voices, from infrasound and seismic resonance to animal and plant communication.

exhibitions.title: Der Suezkanal: Zwischen Ingenieurskunst und Kolonialismus
exhibitions.description: Diaries, photographs and maps from Alois Negrelli's estate show Austria's part in building the Suez Canal and in colonial networks. Shown inside Material Worlds.

exhibitions.title: BEFORE DARK: Viennese Interior Design in the Interwar Period
exhibitions.description: Set designer Anna Viebrock stages MAK collection objects from 1918-1938 as a domestic experiment, exploring how housing and interiors reshaped Vienna after World War I.

exhibitions.title: Modern Fashion: Wiener Werkstätte & Paris
exhibitions.description: Viennese fashion c. 1900–1930: the Wiener Werkstätte's fashion department, reform dress, Emilie Flöge, and the exchange with Paul Poiret's Paris.

exhibitions.title: Creative Aging 2026: Art Is Essential
exhibitions.description: Artwork by older adults living with memory loss, made through the museum's Creative Aging programme of gallery conversations followed by studio practice, with local senior centres and Reframing Care.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1600 21st Street NW, Washington, DC 20009, United States

exhibitions.title: Shahzia Sikander: The Last Post
exhibitions.description: A ten-minute animation in which a British East India Company man dissolves into shifting Indo-Persian miniatures, scored by Pulitzer-winning composer Du Yun.
exhibitions.venue_address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC 20004

exhibitions.title: Harbingers
exhibitions.description: Katherine Steichen Rosing suspends dozens of 10-foot linen columns, inked and charred by candle flame, into a walk-through ghost forest, with video of woodland thickening with carbon.
exhibitions.venue_address: 9 Hillyer Court NW, Washington, DC 20008, United States

exhibitions.title: La Casa en la Montaña
exhibitions.description: Diana Mercado gathers 16 paintings from her London shows Memories of the Andes (2023) and A Tale of the Andes (2025), bridged by a new work and a poem written for the exhibition.
exhibitions.venue_address: 9 Hillyer Court NW, Washington, DC 20008, United States

exhibitions.title: Saodat Ismailova: Melted into the Sun
exhibitions.description: The Uzbek artist's first major US solo show: video works and photographs tracing Central Asia's landscapes, oral histories and Soviet-era ruins.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1050 Independence Ave SW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Re-Inhabiting Conservation: Our Shared Skies
exhibitions.description: Over two dozen artists and writers from six countries take on wildlife conservation through creatures of flight. Curated by Heather McMordie for the nonprofit Creature Conserve.
exhibitions.venue_address: 9 Hillyer Court NW, Washington, DC 20008, United States

exhibitions.title: Sky Hopinka: Kicking the Clouds
exhibitions.description: Photographs, poems and film in which Ho-Chunk artist Sky Hopinka threads together family, language, place and lived Indigenous experience.
exhibitions.venue_address: Constitution Avenue NW, between 3rd and 9th Streets NW, Washington, DC 20565, United States

exhibitions.title: Double Feature: Two Graphic Narratives by Mary Garrard
exhibitions.venue: American University Museum at the Katzen Arts Center
exhibitions.description: A Project Space show of two digital graphic narratives by AU's professor emerita of art history, played out on monitors: a travelling Miami palm tree, and the Odyssey retold around its women.

exhibitions.title: Beyond Words: The Sacred Art of Ayesha Kamal
exhibitions.venue: American University Museum at the Katzen Arts Center
exhibitions.description: Large-scale mixed-media paintings by the contemporary Islamic calligrapher, turning Qur'anic verses and divine names into layered surfaces of metallic leaf, texture and intricate script.

exhibitions.title: American Icon: The US Flag in Art
exhibitions.description: Over 30 works (Jasper Johns, Faith Ringgold, Gordon Parks, Childe Hassam, Dorothea Lange) on how the Stars and Stripes has served as pride, protest and raw material since the late 1800s.
exhibitions.venue_address: Constitution Avenue NW, between 3rd and 9th Streets NW, Washington, DC 20565, United States

exhibitions.title: Observer: The Street Photographs of Norman S. Carr
exhibitions.venue: American University Museum at the Katzen Arts Center
exhibitions.description: Presented by the Alper Initiative for Washington Art: black-and-white street photographs Carr made after a forty-year legal career, building layered compositions out of reflections in DC and abroad.

exhibitions.title: Ahn Chang-Hong: noon-mool
exhibitions.venue: American University Museum at the Katzen Arts Center
exhibitions.description: A major solo show filling the museum's second and third floors with the Korean artist's paintings, sculpture and multimedia, centred on his Taxidermy series on mortality.

exhibitions.title: In the Library: Reimagining America by Design
exhibitions.description: See the Great Depression-era Index of American Design through the eyes of today's college students, in the East Building Library Atrium.
exhibitions.venue_address: Constitution Avenue NW, between 3rd and 9th Streets NW, Washington, DC 20565, United States

exhibitions.title: In Pursuit of Life, Liberty, and Happiness
exhibitions.description: The museum's semiquincentennial blockbuster: 250 objects across all three floors, from Jefferson's writing desk to the 1776 gunboat Philadelphia. Closes at the end of 2026 (exact date not yet announced).
exhibitions.venue_address: 1300 Constitution Ave NW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Out of Bounds
exhibitions.description: Seven Hamiltonian Artists alumni test boundaries across painting, photo, sculpture, video and installation, shown beside Kreeger works by Sam Gilliam, Frank Stella and Simmie Knox.
exhibitions.venue_address: 2401 Foxhall Road NW, Washington, DC 20007, United States

exhibitions.title: Back and Forth
exhibitions.description: Four paintings across six centuries (Titian, Cezanne and Rozeal.) hung together to show how artists answer the art history they inherit.
exhibitions.venue_address: Constitution Avenue NW, between 3rd and 9th Streets NW, Washington, DC 20565, United States

exhibitions.title: Interwoven: A Tradition of Textiles
exhibitions.description: The first exhibition devoted to Hillwood's textiles: 17th-century point de France lace, an 18th-century pearl-trimmed Russian liturgical panel, and new fibre work by Manca Ahlin and Sophia Narrett.
exhibitions.venue_address: 4155 Linnean Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20008, United States

exhibitions.title: Nick Cave: Mammoth
exhibitions.description: Nick Cave remakes the galleries as a dig site: crafted mammoth hides and bones, a video of the beasts come alive, and hundreds of found objects laid out like specimens.
exhibitions.venue_address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC 20004

exhibitions.title: Adam Pendleton: Love, Queen
exhibitions.description: Pendleton's first solo show in Washington, DC fills the second-floor inner ring with new and recent paintings plus a single-channel video, staged for the museum's circular galleries.
exhibitions.venue_address: Independence Ave SW and 7th St SW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Star Power: Photographs from Hollywood's Golden Age by George Hurrell (A Sequel)
exhibitions.description: An encore hang of 20 vintage prints by MGM's in-house glamour portraitist: Garbo, Harlow, Crawford, Gable and Dietrich, lit to look immortal.
exhibitions.venue_address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States

exhibitions.title: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
exhibitions.description: Over 80 quilts trace the Second Great Migration west, carried as warmth, ancestral memory and emblems of cultural survival by Black families settling in California.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1250 New York Ave NW, Washington, DC 20005, United States

exhibitions.title: Water's Edge: The Art of Truman Lowe
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of the American Indian
exhibitions.description: The first major retrospective of Hoocąk sculptor Truman Lowe: nearly 50 works in willow, feathers and pigment that evoke the rivers, waterfalls and canoes of the Wisconsin woodlands.
exhibitions.venue_address: Fourth Street & Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: From the Louvre: Masterpieces of Islamic Art
exhibitions.description: Twenty-six Islamic masterpieces from the Louvre, from Spain to India and the 7th to 19th centuries, including the Mamluk basin known as the Baptistery of Saint Louis.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1050 Independence Ave SW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Avery, Gottlieb & Rothko: By the Sea
exhibitions.description: Around 90 works from the 1920s to the mid-1960s tracing the friendship of Milton Avery, Adolph Gottlieb and Mark Rothko, forged over shared summers in Gloucester. Many shown publicly for the first time.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1600 21st Street NW, Washington, DC 20009, United States

exhibitions.title: Marlo Pascual: Making Something Out of Something
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
exhibitions.description: Marlo Pascual (1972-2020) enlarged, shattered and folded anonymous thrift-store photographs into uncanny Plexiglas sculptures that blur the line between picture and object.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1250 New York Ave NW, Washington, DC 20005, United States

exhibitions.title: Busy Bliss: A Collector's Passion
exhibitions.description: A vivid portrait of Robert Woods Bliss as an early twentieth-century collector, drawn from the estate's own holdings. Special Exhibitions Gallery.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1703 32nd Street NW, Washington, DC 20007, United States

exhibitions.title: Light Is a Plastic Medium: The Photography of Carlotta Corpron
exhibitions.description: Six bodies of work made in Texas between the late 1930s and early 1950s by the abstract photographer and teacher Carlotta Corpron, drawn from a recent gift of 48 prints plus loans.
exhibitions.venue_address: Independence Ave SW and 7th St SW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Remember Me: Picturing African Americans in Early Photography
exhibitions.description: Remarkable early photographs of and by Black Americans that tell powerful stories of identity, resilience, and self-representation. West Building.
exhibitions.venue_address: Constitution Avenue NW, between 3rd and 9th Streets NW, Washington, DC 20565, United States

exhibitions.title: Portrait of Lloyd Patterson
exhibitions.description: A long-term loan portrait of Lloyd Walton Patterson, who travelled to Soviet Russia in 1932 for the film Black and White and stayed, opening up the history of Black Americans in the USSR.
exhibitions.venue_address: 4155 Linnean Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20008, United States

exhibitions.title: Spirit in the Dark: Religion in Black Music, Activism and Popular Culture
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of African American History and Culture
exhibitions.description: Black religious life seen through Johnson Publishing Company photographs from Ebony and Jet, where the holy and the profane meet in music, protest and pop culture.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1400 Constitution Ave NW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Much Here Is Beautiful: Photography Surveys of the U.S. Bicentennial
exhibitions.description: 225 photographs from the NEA's Bicentennial-era survey projects, reuniting a 1970s portrait of America and setting it against federal survey photography going back to the 19th century.
exhibitions.venue_address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC 20004

exhibitions.title: Beverly Pepper: Land Art and Monumental Sculptures
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
exhibitions.description: Gallery-scale sculptures, maquettes and a new film on Beverly Pepper (1922-2020), pairing with her outdoor installation along New York Avenue right outside the museum's door.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1250 New York Ave NW, Washington, DC 20005, United States

exhibitions.title: To Hear Her Speak: Black Women and Shakespeare
exhibitions.description: Curated by Patricia Akhimie, some 100 photographs, playbills, diaries and costumes trace 450 years of Black women engaging Shakespeare, from Phillis Wheatley to Maya Angelou and Toni Morrison.
exhibitions.venue_address: 201 East Capitol Street SE, Washington, DC 20003, United States

exhibitions.title: The Spirit of Invention: Patent Office and Patentees
exhibitions.description: The museum turns its lens on its own building: the early Patent Office, told through portraits of Andrew Jackson, Samuel Morse and Lincoln, the only president to hold a patent.
exhibitions.venue_address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States

exhibitions.title: The Declaration's Promise: A Revolutionary Idea
exhibitions.description: Library collections trace how Americans have argued with, rallied around and reached for the Declaration of Independence and its ideals of equality, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.
exhibitions.venue_address: Thomas Jefferson Building, 10 First Street SE, Washington, DC 20540, United States

exhibitions.title: Big Things for Big Rooms
exhibitions.description: Ten room-swallowing installations trace immersive art from the late 1960s on: Flavin, Gilliam, Irwin, Pape and Long, then Chan, Eliasson, Finch, Johnson and Rottenberg. Five shown here for the first time.
exhibitions.venue_address: Independence Ave SW and 7th St SW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Free and Independent: A Celebration of the Declaration
exhibitions.description: America250 show marking the Declaration's 250th anniversary, in three parts: the Revolution, the preservation of the original parchment, and how Americans have celebrated independence since 1776.
exhibitions.venue_address: 701 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20408, United States (public entrance at Constitution Avenue and 9th Street NW)

exhibitions.title: On Stage: Portraying the Performing Arts
exhibitions.description: More than twenty portraits of musicians, dancers and actors, mostly paintings and sculpture from the past century: Paul Robeson, Katharine Hepburn, Dizzy Gillespie, Maria Callas, LL Cool J.
exhibitions.venue_address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States

exhibitions.title: Homelands
exhibitions.description: What does it mean to have a "homeland" when it's shaped by movement, memory, and change? East Building Mezzanine.
exhibitions.venue_address: Constitution Avenue NW, between 3rd and 9th Streets NW, Washington, DC 20565, United States

exhibitions.title: A Museum in the Making
exhibitions.description: How Charles Lang Freer used his Detroit home as a proving ground for what became the first national art museum of the United States.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1050 Independence Ave SW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Portrait of a Nation: 2025 Honorees
exhibitions.description: New portraits of the 2025 award winners (Jamie Dimon, Temple Grandin, Joy Harjo and Steven Spielberg), including commissions by David Lenz and Kate Capshaw.
exhibitions.venue_address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States

exhibitions.title: Yoshitomo Nara: Sentinels of Stillness
exhibitions.description: Three towering white aluminium heads by Yoshitomo Nara, enlarged from small 2021 clay heads, open the revitalized Sculpture Garden's West Lawn series.
exhibitions.venue_address: Independence Ave SW and 7th St SW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: How Can You Forget Me: Filipino American Stories
exhibitions.description: The overlooked history of a trailblazing Filipino community in California, from the 1910s to the 1970s.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1300 Constitution Ave NW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: We Make History
exhibitions.description: Ahead of the museum's 60th anniversary, this show asks how Washingtonians keep their own history - anchored by the diary of Adam Francis Plummer, with letters, photographs and hands-on archiving stations.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1901 Fort Place SE, Washington, DC 20020, United States

exhibitions.title: "Alive in Many Hands": The American Folklife Center at 50
exhibitions.description: Highlights from the American Folklife Center's 50 years of collecting: recordings, photos and objects on the living traditions of food, play, work and place.
exhibitions.venue_address: Thomas Jefferson Building, 10 First Street SE, Washington, DC 20540, United States

exhibitions.title: Remix: The Collection
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
exhibitions.description: The museum-wide collection installation, rejecting chronology for themes like Photo Credit, Seeing Red and Objectified across six continents and six centuries of women artists.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1250 New York Ave NW, Washington, DC 20005, United States

exhibitions.title: Nation to Nation: Treaties Between the United States and American Indian Nations
exhibitions.venue: National Museum of the American Indian
exhibitions.description: Original treaties on loan from the National Archives, wampum belts and peace medals tell the story of US–Native diplomacy from the colonial era to the present.
exhibitions.venue_address: Fourth Street & Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Meserve Collection Highlights: Modern Prints from Mathew Brady's Portrait Negatives
exhibitions.description: Nine modern prints struck from Mathew Brady's original Civil War-era negatives (Lincoln, Hawthorne, Grant and Emma, Queen of Hawai'i) shown with a glass plate and Brady's wooden storage box.
exhibitions.venue_address: 8th and G Streets NW, Washington, DC 20001, United States

exhibitions.title: ¡Puro Ritmo! The Musical Journey of Salsa
exhibitions.description: From the streets of Havana to the dance floors of New York and beyond, this bilingual show traces how salsa grew into a defining sound of the United States.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1300 Constitution Ave NW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: Do Ho Suh: Public Figures
exhibitions.description: On the Freer plaza facing the National Mall, a monumental empty plinth held aloft by hundreds of small striding figures, questioning who monuments are for.

exhibitions.title: Bison: Standing Strong

exhibitions.venue_address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20560, United States

exhibitions.title: From These Lands: Sharing Our Natural and Cultural Heritage
exhibitions.description: More than 600 specimens and cultural belongings from all 50 states, DC and five US territories: fossils, minerals and treasures chosen to represent every corner of the country.

exhibitions.title: Photographic Memory: Fifty Years of Collecting

exhibitions.title: Adorned in Gold: Japanese Lacquer from the Jacqueline Avant Collection
exhibitions.description: Edo-period maki-e lacquer from the collection of philanthropist Jacqueline Avant: gold-on-black hairpins, combs, boxes and a princess's litter.

exhibitions.title: Tinker Tinker: Printmakers at Work
exhibitions.description: An intimate look at how artists like Pablo Picasso, Mary Cassatt, and Rembrandt experimented, revised, and problem-solved through printmaking. West Building.

exhibitions.title: Women and the Index of American Design
exhibitions.description: Nearly 50 drawings examine women's roles in the Depression-era art project that sought to document American designs in applied, decorative, and folk art. East Building.

exhibitions.title: Gold: Celebrating 50 Years of Beauty at Hillwood
